body.text: Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhāna-vyūham Sūtram
body.translated_text: <s>Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhāna-vyūha Sūtra</s> (The Sūtra of the Empowerment-Array of All Tathāgatas)

body.text:
evaṃ mayā śrutamekasmin samaye potalakaparvate āryāvalokiteśvarāyatane divyamaṇiratnaśrīindranīlamaye puṣpasaṃstṛte devasiṃhāsane bhagavān sārdhaṃ mahatā bhikṣusaṅghena pañcamātrairbhikṣuśataiḥ sarvairarhadbhiḥ kṣīṇāsravaiścetovaśitāprāptaiḥ saddharmapāraṃgataiśca sārdhaṃ bodhisattvaiḥ sarvaiḥ mahākaruṇājñānaprāptaiḥ sarvaiḥ ekajātipratibaddhairdvijātibhyāṃ ca trijātibhirdaśajātibhirviśatijātibhistriṃśajjātibhiḥ śatajātibhirvā pratibaddhaiḥ sarvaiḥ aṣṭaphalaprāptairdaśabhūmisthitaiḥ tad yathā āryāvalokiteśvareṇa maṃjuśriyāvimalaketunā ratnaśriyā vajraketunā vimalaprabheṇa candanena amṛtaketunā evaṃpramukhaiḥ saptaśataiḥ bodhisattvaiḥ sārdham upāsakopāsikābhiḥ sarvaiśca vyākṛtaiḥ samādhiprāptaiḥ nānālokadhātubhiḥ sannipatitaiḥ pañcasahasraiḥ sarvaiḥ gandharvaśatasahasraiḥ pūrvabuddhaparyupāsitaiḥ
tathāgataprātihāryadṛṣṭaiḥ sārdhaṃ sarvābhiḥ mahāyakṣiṇībhiḥ bodhisattvajñānaprāptābhiḥ vyākaraṇaprāptābhiravaivartikābhiḥ anaupamyayā vimalaprabhayā ca prabhāvatyā bhīmaśriyā yakṣiṇyā ca evaṃpramukhābhiraśītyā mahāyakṣiṇībhiḥ / śatakratubrahmavaiśravaṇa dhṛtarāṣṭravirūḍhakavirūpākṣamaṇibhadraputrapūrṇabhadrāḥ etaiśca lokapālaiḥ sārdhaṃ niṣaṇṇo 'bhūt /
body.translated_text:
Thus have I heard. At one time, on Mount <s>Potalaka</s>, in the abode of the Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, on a divine lion-throne made of radiant <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire) jewels and strewn with flowers, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was seated together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, five hundred <s>bhikṣus</s> in number, all <s>arhats</s>, with outflows extinguished, having attained mastery of mind, gone to the far shore of the True <s>Dharma</s>; together with <s>bodhisattvas</s>, all having attained the knowledge of great compassion, all bound to a single birth, or bound by two births, three births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, or a hundred births, all having attained the eight fruits, established on the ten stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) — namely, the Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, <s>Vimalaketu</s>, <s>Ratnaśrī</s>, <s>Vajraketu</s>, <s>Vimalaprabha</s>, <s>Candana</s>, <s>Amṛtaketu</s>, and other such foremost ones — together with seven hundred <s>bodhisattvas</s>; together with male and female lay-followers (<s>upāsaka</s> and <s>upāsikā</s>), all having received prophecies [of future enlightenment], having attained <s>samādhi</s>, gathered from various world-realms, five thousand in number; together with all the hundreds of thousands of <s>gandharvas</s>, who had served former <s>Buddhas</s>,
who had witnessed the miracles of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; together with all the great <s>yakṣiṇīs</s>, who had attained <s>bodhisattva</s>-knowledge, who had received prophecies, who were irreversible — <s>Anaupamyā</s>, <s>Vimalaprabhā</s>, <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, <s>Bhīmaśrī</s> the <s>yakṣiṇī</s>, and other such foremost ones — together with eighty great <s>yakṣiṇīs</s>; together with <s>Śatakratu</s> (Indra), <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, <s>Maṇibhadra</s>, <s>Pūtra</s>, and <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s> — together with these world-protectors (<s>lokapālas</s>) he was seated.

body.text: atha taiḥ sarvaistathāgataṃ siṃhāsananiṣaṇṇaṃ jñātvā svakasvakaiḥ kuśalamūlaistathāgataṃ divyālaṃkāravastrapuṣpamālyadhūpavilepanavādyaśabdena mānitaḥ pūjitaḥ śatasahasrakoṭiśaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya arcitaśca / tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān sarvasattvamahākaruṇājñānasthitaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpanno 'bhūt / tena samādhidhāraṇabalena trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātavaḥ ābhayā avabhāsitā abhūvan / sarvarūpāṇi sphuṭitāni / ye ca sattvā jātyandhāḥ cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi paśyanti sma / vadhirāḥ śrotreṇa śabdān śṛṇvanti sma / rogaspṛṣṭā vigatarogā bhavanti sma / nagnāśca vastrāvṛtā vabhūvuḥ / unmattāḥ smṛtiṃ pratilabhante sma / hīnakāyāḥ paripūrṇendriyā babhūvuḥ / daridra dhanāni pratilabhante sma / sattvānāṃ yaḥ khalu dhanavastubhogavihīna āsīt sa dhanavastubhogasampanno 'bhūt / sarvasattvāḥ sarvasukhasamarpitāḥ sarvāśāparipūrṇā abhūvan / trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau ye kecit sattvā anuśāsanadharmaśravaṇāya yena bhagavān tenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya upasaṃkrāntāḥ / ye sattvāḥ
body.translated_text: Then, all of them, knowing the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be seated on the lion-throne, with their own respective roots of merit, honored and worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s> with divine ornaments, garments, flowers, garlands, incense, ointments, and the sound of music, circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of times, and venerated him. At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered into a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Abiding in the Knowledge of Great Compassion for All Beings.' By the power of that <s>samādhi</s> and <s>dhāraṇī</s>, the great trichiliocosm was illuminated with radiance. All forms became manifest. Those beings who were blind from birth saw forms with their eyes. The deaf heard sounds with their ears. Those afflicted by disease became free of disease. The naked became covered with garments. The insane regained their mindfulness. Those with deficient bodies became complete in their faculties. The destitute obtained wealth. Whatever being had been deprived of wealth, possessions, and enjoyments became endowed with wealth, possessions, and enjoyments. All beings were bestowed with all happiness and had all their wishes fulfilled. Whatever beings there were in the great trichiliocosm who wished to hear the <s>Dharma</s> of instruction approached with joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Those beings who

body.text: devabhūtāste sarvadevasukhaṃ saṃprahāya buddhānusmṛtiṃ kṛtvā dharmaśravaṇāya yena bhagavān tena upasaṃkrāntāḥ / ye sattvā manuṣyabhūtāste ca manuṣyasukhaṃ parityajya dharmaśravaṇakāmāya yena bhagavāṃstena upasaṃkrāntāḥ / ye sattvā nāgayakṣarākṣasapretapiśācabhūtāste buddhānusmṛtiṃ prāpya sarvasattveṣu maitracittā bhūtvā kāyacittasukhaṃ labdhvā dharmaśravaṇāya yena bhagavān tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ / ye sattvā yamaloke andhatamisrāyāṃ jātāste 'pi buddhānubhāvena ekakṣaṇaṃ smṛtiṃ labdhvā parasparaṃ saṃjānate sma / te mahātamisrābhyaḥ parimuktā babhūvuḥ / sarve satvāḥ parasparaṃ maitracittā babhūvuḥ / teṣāmupakleśāḥ kṣīṇā abhūvan / tena khalu samayena mahāpṛthivī ṣaḍ vikāraṃ prakampate unnamati avanamati sma / atha tasyāṃ parṣadi maṃjuśrīkumārabhūtaḥ sanniṣaṇṇaḥ san bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāryāvalokiteśvarametadavocat / kulaputra mahābodhisattvaparṣadi avabhāsitāyāṃ mahāparṣadaḥ pūrvanimittaṃ parisphuṭam / anekabodhisattvakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ ca vyākaraṇaṃ prakaṭitam / dharmamahāvākyasya pūrvanimittaṃ saṃdṛśyate / kulaputra anekānāṃ ca bodhisattvakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ sarvāśāparipūri mahājñānapratilambho bhaviṣyati / tat kulaputra sattvānāṃ kāruṇyamutpādya hitāya sukhāya yāvadanuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpanāya tathāgataṃ paripṛccha /
body.translated_text: had become gods, having abandoned all divine pleasures and recollecting the <s>Buddha</s>, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. Those beings who were humans, having relinquished human pleasures, desiring to hear the <s>Dharma</s>, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Those beings who were <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, and <s>bhūtas</s>, having attained the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>, having become benevolent-minded toward all beings, having obtained happiness of body and mind, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. Those beings who had been born in the dense darkness of the world of <s>Yama</s> — even they, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, having obtained mindfulness for a single moment, recognized one another. They became freed from the great darkness. All beings became benevolent-minded toward one another. Their afflictions were extinguished. At that time, the great earth trembled with six kinds of tremors — it rose up and sank down. Then, in that assembly, the youthful <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, who was seated there, addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> with these words: Noble son, in this great assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, which has been illuminated, the portent of the great assembly has become manifest. The prophecy of countless <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s> has been revealed. The portent of the great utterance of <s>Dharma</s> is being seen. Noble son, the attainment of great knowledge fulfilling all wishes will come about for countless <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore, noble son, having generated compassion for beings, for their benefit, for their happiness, and for establishing them in unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), inquire of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: santi kulaputra sattvāḥ paścime kāle paścime samaye bhaviṣyanti pāpakāriṇo daridrāḥ kṛśā durvarṇaśarīrā jarāvyādhiparipīḍitāḥ parīttabhogā aparibhāvitakāyā alpāyuṣkā alpabuddhayo rāgadveṣamohaparipīḍitāḥ / teṣāmarthāya kulaputra tathāgatamadhyeṣaya dharmadeśanāyai tat te kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati dīrgharātraṃ sattvānā[marthāya] hitāya sukhāya sarvāvyādhipraśamanāya sarvapāpanivāraṇāya sarvapāpapraśamanāya sarvaśāparipūraṇārthaṃ yāvadanuttaraparinirvāṇārtham /
body.translated_text: There are, noble son, beings who in the final age, in the final time, will be evildoers, destitute, emaciated, of ill-complexioned bodies, tormented by old age and disease, of meager possessions, with uncultivated bodies, of short lifespan, of little understanding, tormented by passion, hatred, and delusion. For their sake, noble son, beseech the <s>Tathāgata</s> for a <s>Dharma</s> teaching. That will be for you a benefit for beings throughout the long night — for their welfare, for their happiness, for the pacification of all diseases, for the prevention of all evil, for the calming of all evil, for the fulfillment of all wishes, and for the attainment of unsurpassed <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: I
body.translated_text: I

body.text: atha āryāvalokiśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo daśadiśamavalokya gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatakoṭīrmamanasi kurvan yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya triḥpradakṣiṇīkṛtya paṃcamaṇḍalena praṇipatya bhagavantametadavocat / santi bhagavan sattvāḥ paścime kāle bhaviṣyanti jarāvyādhiśokamṛtyu[duḥkha]kālamṛtyuparipīḍitāḥ kṛśā durvarṇā alpāyuṣkāḥ parīttabhogā aparibhāvitakāyāste parasparāṇi mātsaryadauḥśīlyacittatayā ghātayiṣyanti parasparāṇi dhanabhogaiśvaryāṇyāpahariṣyanti hāsyalāsyanāṭyakrīḍābhiratāḥ anitye nityasaṃjñinaḥ aśubhe śubhasaṃjñinaḥ / te taddhetau tannidānā sattvā nānāprakārairviha[ga]narakatiryagyoniyamalokeṣu copapatsyante / tat teṣāmahaṃ bhagavan arthāya hitāya sarvāśāparipūrarṇārthaṃ yāvat tathāgatajñānāharaṇārthaṃ buddhakṣetropapattaye sarvapāpanivāraṇārthaṃ tathāgatamadhyeṣyāmi / bhāṣasva bhagavan bhāṣasva sugato nāsti tathāgatasya tajjñānaṃ yadaviditam adṛṣṭam aśrutam avijñātameva / bahavo bhagavan bodhisattvabhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā devanāgā yakṣagandharvāsurakinnarāśca samāgatā dharmasāṃkathyaṃ śrotukāmāḥ pūrvabuddhaparyupāsitāḥ saprajñā jātāḥ te nirāśībhūtā prakramiṣyanti /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, having gazed in the ten directions, bringing to mind <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, joined his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, circumambulated him three times, prostrated with the five points of contact, and addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these words: There are, <s>Bhagavān</s>, beings who in the final age will be tormented by old age, disease, sorrow, death, untimely death, emaciated, of ill complexion, of short lifespan, of meager possessions, with uncultivated bodies — they will, with minds of jealousy and moral corruption, kill one another, rob one another of wealth, possessions, and sovereignty, delighting in laughter, dance, theater, and play, perceiving the impermanent as permanent, perceiving the impure as pure. Due to that cause and condition, those beings will be reborn in various states — in the realms of animals, <s>naraka</s> (hell), the animal realm, and the world of <s>Yama</s>. Therefore, <s>Bhagavān</s>, for their sake, for their benefit, for the fulfillment of all wishes, and for the attainment of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, for birth in a <s>Buddha</s>-field, for the prevention of all evil, I beseech the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Speak, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Speak, <s>Sugata</s>! There is no knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> that is unknown, unseen, unheard, or unperceived. Many <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, <s>upāsikās</s>, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>kinnaras</s> have assembled, wishing to hear the <s>Dharma</s> discourse, having served former <s>Buddhas</s>, born with wisdom — they will depart in despair [if nothing is taught].

body.text: atha te sarve yathā samāgatāḥ parṣat paṃcamaṇḍalena praṇipatya ekakaṇṭhena evamāhuḥ / sādhu bhagavan bhāṣasva bhagavan bhāṣasva sugataḥ /
body.translated_text: Then all those who had assembled in the assembly prostrated with the five points of contact and spoke with one voice: Excellent, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Speak, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Speak, <s>Sugata</s>!

body.text: atha bhagavān dvirapi trirapi adhyeṣaṇāṃ viditvā daśadiśamavalokya valgumaṇojñasvareṇāryāvalokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat / asti kulaputra sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānsattvāvalokanabuddhakṣetrasandarśanavyūho nāma samādhiḥ yo mayā pūrvaṃ prathamacittotpādamupādāya śrutaḥ / sukusumajyotiḥsandarśanasya tathāgatasyāntikāt śrutaḥ / tat sahaśravaṇādeva tasya samādhernāmadheyasya navatīnāṃ sattvakoṭīnāṃ tathāgatajñānapratilambho 'bhūt / te sarve ca vyākṛtāstathāgatairnānābyuddhakṣetreṣu / mayā ca kulaputra vyākaraṇamanuprāptam / tat smarāmyahaṃ kulaputra divyena tathāgatajñānena triṃśatyā tathāgatasahasrairayaṃ dharmaparyāyo bhāṣitaḥ sattvānāmarthāya / sarvatra tvamevāryāvalokiteśvara tathagatādhyeṣakaḥ maṃjuśriyaśca kumārabhūtaḥ / ayaṃ ca yathā samāgatā sarvabodhisattvānāṃ parṣad bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā parṣad[ete sarve]śrutvā mānanāṃ pūjanāṃ kurvanti sma / tataścānekāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi vyākaraṇaṃ pratilabhante sma / bodhisattvasamādhīnāṃ ca lābhino bhavanti / sarvakāmaṃ gatāḥ kṛtasarvāśāḥ samṛdhyante vigatavyādhayaḥ saṃvṛttā paripakvakuśalamūlāḥ sarvāvaraṇaprahīṇā abhirūpaprāsādikadarśanīyā dhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgārasamṛddhāḥ sarvarājarājaputrāmatyābhinandanīyāḥ sarvasattvairvandanīyāḥ
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having recognized the entreaty a second and a third time, surveying the ten directions, with a sweet and pleasing voice spoke thus to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>: There exists, son of good family, a <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) called '<s>Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhāna-sattvāvalokana-buddhakṣetrasandarśana-vyūha</s>' (The Array of the Empowerment of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the Beholding of Beings, and the Vision of <s>Buddha</s>-fields), which was heard by me previously, from the very first generation of the mind of awakening (<s>prathamacittotpāda</s>). It was heard from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sukusumajyotiḥsandarśana</s> (Vision of Excellent Flower-Light). Indeed, merely upon hearing the name of that <s>samādhi</s>, ninety <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of beings attained the realization of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge. And all of them received prophecies from the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in various <s>Buddha</s>-fields. And I too, son of good family, obtained a prophecy [of future awakening]. I recall, son of good family, with divine <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, that this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse of the Dharma) was proclaimed by thirty thousand <s>Tathāgatas</s> for the benefit of beings. And everywhere, you yourself, Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, were the one who entreated the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, along with <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince (<s>kumārabhūta</s>). And this assembly of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> that has gathered here, the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, and <s>upāsikās</s> — all of them, having heard, performed veneration and worship. And thereupon innumerable <s>koṭi-niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of beings obtained prophecies [of future awakening]. And they became recipients of <s>bodhisattva samādhis</s>. They attained all desires, fulfilled all hopes, prospered, became free from diseases, their wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) matured, all obstructions (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) were abandoned, they became handsome, pleasing, and beautiful to behold, endowed with abundance of wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses, worthy of the delight of all kings, princes, and ministers, and worthy of reverence by all beings

body.text: smṛtimantaḥ prajñāvantaḥ buddhe dhama saṃghe abhedyaprasādena samanvāgatā dhṛtimantaḥ āyurvarṇatejobalarathāmavantaḥ sarvākāravaropetāḥ samanvāgatāḥ / na ca kadācit priyaviprayogaṃ na priyavyasanaṃ saṃvṛttam / evaṃ kulaputra bahuguṇasasanvāgatāste kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaraśca bhaviṣyanti / yadā saddharmaparyāyaṃ paṃcamaṇḍalena praṇipatya puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacchatradhvajapatākaiḥ samalaṃkṛtya namo buddhāyeti kṛtvā namaskariṣyanti sādhukāraṃ dāsyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti vācāpayiṣyanti likhiṣyanti likhāpayiṣyanti paramagauravaṃ cittamutpādya tasya dharmabhāṇakasyāntike te dṛṣṭa eva dharme sarvasaguṇasamanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti abhirūpāḥ prāsādikā darśanīyā vigatavyādhayo dīrghāyuṣkāḥ sthirabuddhayaḥ smṛtimantaḥ dhṛtimantaḥ sarvarājānāṃ sarvarājñīnāṃ rājaputrāmātyānāṃ sarvaśatrūṇāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ cābhinandanīyā bhaviṣyanti vandanīyāḥ satkaraṇīyāḥ / prabhūtavittopakaraṇā bhaviṣyanti / candanagandhaḥ cāsya mukhāt pravāsyati / nīlotpalasadṛśanetro bhaviṣyati / rātrindivaṃ cāsya buddhabodhisattvadarśanaṃ bhaviṣyati / sarvāvaraṇaṃ cāsya kṣayaṃ cāsyanti paṃcānantaryaprabhṛtayaḥ kṛtvā / devatāśāsya
body.translated_text: possessed of mindfulness, endowed with wisdom, possessed of unshakeable faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s>, steadfast, endowed with long life, beauty, radiance, strength, and eloquence, possessed of all excellent qualities and marks. And never did separation from the beloved occur, nor loss of the beloved. Thus, son of good family, those sons or daughters of good family who worship this true <s>dharmaparyāya</s> with the five-limbed prostration, adorn it with flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, ointments, parasols, banners, and flags, pay homage saying 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!', give exclamations of approval, retain it, recite it, cause it to be recited, write it, cause it to be written, generate a mind of supreme reverence before that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher — they will become endowed with all good qualities in this very life: handsome, pleasing, beautiful to behold, free from diseases, long-lived, of firm understanding, possessed of mindfulness, steadfast, worthy of the delight of all kings, all queens, princes, and ministers, of all enemies, and of all beings — worthy of reverence and honor. They will be endowed with abundant wealth and resources. The fragrance of sandalwood will emanate from their mouths. They will have eyes like blue lotuses (<s>nīlotpala</s>). Day and night they will have visions of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. And all their obstructions will be exhausted, including those of the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) acts. Deities

rakṣiṣyanti / maraṇakāle cāsya buddhadarśanaṃ bodhisattvadarśana bhaviṣyati / na īrṣyāluko na vikṣepacittaṃ kālaṃ kariṣyati / yāvaccyutaḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapadyate vyākṛtāste mayā kulaputra saṃmukhavyākaraṇena / dṛṣṭo 'haṃ taiḥ satkṛto mānitaḥ / na taiḥ saṃśayamutpādayitavyam / bodhau ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayiṣyanti satkṛtya likhiṣyanti likhāpayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti pūjayiṣyanti udgrahīṣyanti nāmadheyaṃ ca
śroṣyanti / bodhisattva iti sa manasi kṛtvā satkartavyaḥ / yenāsya pūvakarmavipākenāsya rūpavaikalyaṃ bhogavaikalyaṃ buddhivaikalyaṃ paribhāṣyaṃ ca priyaviprayogaṃ ca rājyakṣobhaṃ ca te asya samādheranubhāvena śravaṇena kecicchīrṣarogeṇa kecidbhaktacchedena kecit kucelābhidhāraṇena kecit kāyacittapīḍena kecit duḥkhasaṃsparśaśayyākalpanena kecit paribhāṣyeṇa sarvaṃ tat karmāvaraṇaṃ kṣayaṃ yāsyanti / tena cavaṃ cittamutpādayitavyaṃ pūrvaṃ mayā saṃsāre saṃsaradbhiḥ pāpamakuśalaṃ sattveṣu nānāprakāramupacitaṃ taṃ pratideśayāmi āviṣkaromi na praticchādayāmi / buddhe dharme saṃghe abhedyaprasādacittamutpādayitavyam / yeca tasya kulaputrasya kuluduhiturvā chedabhogaphalaṃ saṃvartanīyaṃ
body.translated_text: will protect them. And at the time of death, they will have visions of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. They will not die with a jealous or distracted mind. And upon departing, they will be reborn in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Land of Bliss). They have been prophesied by me, son of good family, with face-to-face prophecy. I have been seen by them, honored and revered. They should not give rise to any doubt regarding awakening — those who will retain this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, who will write and have it written with reverence, recite it, worship it, take it up, and hear its name. Regarding such a person, thinking 'This is a <s>bodhisattva</s>,' one should honor them. Whatever karmic ripening due to previous actions — bodily deformity, loss of resources, deficiency of understanding, being reviled, separation from the beloved, or political disturbances — all of that, through the power of this <s>samādhi</s>, through hearing [it]: for some through headache, for some through interruption of food, for some through wearing poor garments, for some through physical and mental affliction, for some through experiencing an uncomfortable bed, for some through being reviled — all those karmic obstructions (<s>karmāvaraṇa</s>) will be exhausted. And by such a person, this thought should be generated: 'Previously, while I was wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>, I accumulated various kinds of sinful and unwholesome [deeds] toward beings — that I confess, that I reveal, and I do not conceal.' An unshakeable mind of faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s> should be generated. And whatever karmic obstruction of that son or daughter of good family would have resulted in the cutting off of resources

body.text: karmāvaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati buddhe vā dharme vā saṃghe vā śrāvakapratyekabuddhe vā mātāpitṛbhirvā [pāpa]karmakṛtamupacittaṃ bhaviṣyati tat sarva parikṣayaṃ yāsyati / mahaiśvaryasamṛddho bhaviṣyati / ye ca tasya kulaputrasya ca kuladuhiturvā duḥkhanārakavedanīyaṃ karmāvaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati priyaviprayogasaṃvartanīyaṃ jātyandhasaṃvartanīyaṃ strīsaṃvartanīyaṃ dvivyaṃjanasaṃvartanīyaṃ īrṣyāmānakrodhavaśena yamalokapretatiryagyonisaṃvartanīyaṃ tat sarvaṃ parikṣayaṃ yāsyati / evaṃ kulaputra sarvaguṇākaro 'yaṃ samādheḥ /
body.translated_text: — evil <s>karma</s> accumulated against the <s>Buddha</s>, or the <s>Dharma</s>, or the <s>Saṅgha</s>, or the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, or against mother and father — all of that will be completely exhausted. They will become endowed with great sovereignty and prosperity. And whatever karmic obstruction of that son or daughter of good family would have resulted in the suffering of hell realms, in separation from the beloved, in blindness from birth, in being born as a woman, in being born as a eunuch, or — through the power of jealousy, pride, and anger — would have resulted in rebirth in the world of <s>Yama</s>, the realm of hungry ghosts (<s>pretas</s>), or animal births: all of that will be completely exhausted. Thus, son of good family, this <s>samādhi</s> is a mine of all good qualities.

body.text: asti kulaputrāsya dharmaparyāyasya cirasthitikarāḥ / teṣāṃ ca kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṛṇāṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptāni / sarveṣāṃ guṇānāṃ sarvaśāparipūrakarāṇi mahābhogaiśvaryasukhakarāṇi sarvacintitaprārthitasamṛddhikarāṇi sarvakarmakṣayaṃkarāṇi sarvākālamṛtyuduḥsvapnasarvavyādhipraśamanakarāṇī sarvayuddhajayaṃkarāṇi āyurvarṇabalavīryasthāmakarāṇi sarvayakṣabhūtamanuṣyavaśaṃkarāṇi sarvajvarāviṣādakapraśamanakarāṇi yāvadvyākaraṇapratilaṃbhakarāṇi dhāraṇīmantrapadāni yāni śrutvā dhāritvā vācitvā satkaritvā likhitvā likhapayitvā guptaye / sa te kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaraśca sarvānetān guṇān pratilabhante / atha tasmin samaye iyaṃ mahāpṛthivī ṣaḍvikāramakaṃpata / sā ca yathā samāgatā parṣat tathāgataṃ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyaduṣyayugaiḥ saṃcchādya sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu bhagavan katamāni tāni mantrapadāni /
body.translated_text: There exist, son of good family, <s>dhāraṇī-mantra</s> words (<s>dhāraṇīmantrapadāni</s>) that bring about the long endurance of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>; that serve as protection, shelter, and safeguard for those sons and daughters of good family; that fulfill all qualities; that bring about great prosperity, sovereignty, and happiness; that bring about the accomplishment of all that is contemplated and desired; that bring about the exhaustion of all <s>karma</s>; that bring about the pacification of all untimely death, evil dreams, and all diseases; that bring about victory in all battles; that bring about long life, beauty, strength, vigor, and firmness; that bring about the subjugation of all <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>bhūtas</s>, and non-humans; that bring about the pacification of all fevers, poisons, and grief; and that bring about even the attainment of prophecy [of future awakening]. Having heard, retained, recited, honored, written, and had them written for protection — those sons or daughters of good family will obtain all these qualities. Then at that time, this great earth trembled with six kinds of quaking. And that assembly which had gathered together covered the <s>Tathāgata</s> with flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, and pairs of garments, and gave their approval: Excellent! Excellent, <s>Bhagavān</s>! What are those <s>mantra</s> words?

body.text: namaḥ sarvatathāgatānām tadyathābuddhe subuddhe śuddhamate / loke viloke lokātikrānte / sattvāvalokane sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhite / sarvaśāparipūraṇe dyutindhare narake ca pūjite tathāgatajñānadade tathāgatādhiṣṭhāne ca / sarvalokaḥ sukhī bhavatu / pūrvakarma kṣapaya / mama
body.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>! Namely: O <s>Buddha</s>, O Well-Awakened One, O Pure-Minded One! O World-Knower, O World-Transcender, O Transcender of the World! O Beholder of Beings, O One Empowered by the Empowerment of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>! O Fulfiller of All [Wishes], O Bearer of Splendor, O One Worshipped even in the Hells! O Bestower of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, O <s>Tathāgata</s>-Empowerment! May all the world be happy! Exhaust [my] former <s>karma</s>! For me,

body.text: imāni tāni kulaputrāho mantrapadāni triṃśatyā tathāgatasahasrairbhāṣitāni adhiṣṭhitāni mayāpyetarhi bhāṣitā[ni] sarvasattvānāmarthāya hitāya sukhāya rakṣāvaraṇaguptaye sarvavyādhipraśamanakarāṇi buddhakṣetropapattaye / yaḥ kaścit parṣa evaṃ jānīyuḥ kathaṃ nu vayaṃ sarvānetān tathāgatabhāṣitān guṇān pratilabheya tena kalyamevotthāya sarvasattvānāṃ dayācittena karūṇācittena maitracittena īrṣyāmānamrakṣakrodhaparivarjitena ekāgracittena buddhasyodāratarāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā daśadiśaṃ sarvatathāgatānāṃ namaskṛtvā yathākāmaṃ guṇān manasikṛtya aṣṭaśataṃ japya puṣpamekaikaṃ tathāgate deyam / tatastasya sarvāśāsamṛddhirbhaviṣyati / svapne ca tathāgatadarśanaṃ bhaviṣyati / yaṃ varam icchati taṃ labhate / maraṇakāle ca tathāgatadarśanaṃ bhaviṣyati / cyutvā sukhāvatyāṃ ca lokadhātau upapatsyate / āyurbalavarṇaviryasamanvāgataḥ / sarvaśatravaścāsya vaśagāmino bhaviṣyanti /
body.translated_text: These, O sons of good family, are the <s>mantra</s>-padas spoken and empowered by thirty thousand <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and now spoken by me as well, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all beings, for their protection, shielding, and safeguarding, for the pacification of all diseases, and for birth in a <s>Buddha</s>-field. Whoever in the assembly should think thus: 'How may we obtain all these qualities spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' — that person, having risen early, with a mind of compassion toward all beings, with a mind of loving-kindness, free from jealousy, pride, envy, and anger, with a one-pointed mind, having performed the most excellent worship of the <s>Buddha</s>, having bowed to all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions, having brought to mind the desired qualities, having recited [the mantra] eight hundred times, should offer flowers one by one to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Then all his wishes will be fulfilled. In dreams he will see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Whatever boon he desires, he obtains. At the time of death, he will see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. After passing away, he will be reborn in the <s>Sukhāvatī</s> world-realm. He will be endowed with longevity, strength, beauty, and vigor. And all his enemies will come under his power.

body.text: asyāṃ khalu punardhāraṇyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ ṣaṣṭīnāṃ ca prāṇisahasrāṇāmanutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntipratilaṃbho 'bhūt / sarve ca sarva[karmā] varaṇavinirmuktāḥ sarvābhiprāyaparipūrṇāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ /
body.translated_text: When this <s>dhāraṇī</s> was being spoken, sixty thousand living beings attained the <s>kṣānti</s> (forbearance) regarding the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti</s>). And all became freed from all <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> (karmic obscurations) and had all their aspirations fulfilled.

body.text: II
body.translated_text: II

body.text: atha khalu vajrapāṇirbodhisattvo daśadiśaṃ vyavalokya bhagavantametadavocat / asti bhagavan abhayatejaṃ nāma dhāraṇī bodhisattvānāṃ pratijñā yā mayā abhayavyūharājasya tathāgatasyāntikādudgṛhītā / udgṛhya sarvasattvebhyaḥ prakāśitā / tataḥ punaḥ bhagavan nābhijānābhi yasya svapne 'pi sā dhāraṇī karṇapuṭe nipatitāntargatā tasya syāccharīre daurbalyaṃ vā kleśo vā vyādhirvā jvaro vā kāyaśūlaṃ vā cittapīḍā vā akālamṛtyurvā udakaṃ vā śastraṃ vā viṣaṃ vā garaṃ vā ḍākinī vā bhūto vā yakṣo vā śatravo vā manuṣyā vāmanuṣyā vā viheṭhaṃ vā kartuṃ hiṃsāṃ vā vidhātuṃ vā nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate / tadanujānātu bhagavan yadahaṃ bodhisattvapratijñāmudrāṃ dāsyāmi / teṣāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāṃ dharmaśrāvaṇikānāmarthāya śrotṝṇāṃ mānayitṝṇāṃ pūjayitṝṇāṃ dhārayitṝṇāṃ vācayitṝṇāṃ sarvāśāparipūrakarāṇi /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, having gazed in the ten directions, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these words: There is, <s>Bhagavān</s>, a <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Abhayateja</s> (Fearless Splendor), the pledge of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, which was received by me from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Abhayavyūharāja</s>. Having received it, I proclaimed it to all beings. Moreover, <s>Bhagavān</s>, I do not know of anyone into whose ear this <s>dhāraṇī</s> has entered, even in a dream, who could be afflicted with bodily weakness, or mental affliction, or disease, or fever, or bodily pain, or mental distress, or untimely death, or [harm from] water, weapons, poison, venom, <s>ḍākinīs</s>, <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, enemies, humans, or non-humans — that they could harm or injure him — such a possibility does not exist. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> give permission that I bestow the <s>bodhisattva</s>-pledge-seal, for the benefit of those <s>Dharma</s> preachers, <s>Dharma</s> listeners, hearers, those who honor, worship, retain, and recite [this <s>dhāraṇī</s>] — for the fulfillment of all their wishes.

body.text: namaḥ sarvabuddhānām / sarvabodhisattvānāmarhantānām / tadyathā om vajradhara vajradhara vajrakāya vajrabala vajrateja / hum hum / vajrapāṇe
body.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s>! To all <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>arhats</s>! <s>Tadyathā</s>: <s>Oṃ vajradhara vajradhara vajrakāya vajrabala vajrateja</s> / <s>hūṃ hūṃ</s> / O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>

body.text: tathāgatājñāṃ pālaya / smara pratijñām / sarvavyādhiṃ sarvapāpāni nāśaya / dehi me yathepsitaṃ varam / mama
body.translated_text: uphold the command of the <s>Tathāgata</s>! Remember the pledge! Destroy all diseases and all sins! Grant me the desired boon! For me —

body.translated_text: Whatever we pray for, may that very thing be accomplished! <s>He he</s> / <s>turu turu</s> / Come, come! Do not delay! Show the <s>vajra</s>-body, show the <s>vajra</s>-body! By the empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: asyāṃ dhāraṇyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyām iyaṃ mahāpṛthivī unmajjanimajjanaṃ karotu / sarve ca yakṣarākṣasāḥ saṃbhrāntāḥ sarve ca devā yāvad manuṣyāmanuṣyā vismayamāpannāḥ sādhukāraṃ pradadati / sādhu sādhu mahāsattvāḥ paramasiddhāni imāni dhāraṇīmantrapadāni bhāṣitāni / atha vajrapāṇibodhisattvo bhagavantametadavocat / yaḥ kaścid bhadanta bhagavan bodhisattvabhūmimabhiprārthayate dhanadhānyabhogaiśvaryaṃ rājyaṃ vidyādharatvam āyurbalavīryadīrghāyuṣkatvaṃ tena śuklāṣṭamyāṃ śvetacandanamayo vajradharaḥ kāryaḥ aṭṭahāsaḥ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitaḥ / sadhātukahṛdayaṃ kartavyam / sadhātukaṃ vajra[dharaṃ] samāśvāsakaṃ vidyādharaṃ dhūpadahyamānaṃ śucinā ahorātroṣitena kāryam / tato 'ṣṭamyāṃ pūrvasecaṃ
body.translated_text: When this <s>dhāraṇī</s> was being spoken, this great earth rose up and sank down. All <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> were terrified. All <s>devas</s>, including humans and non-humans, were filled with wonder and uttered approval: 'Excellent, excellent, O great beings! These supremely accomplished <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>mantra</s>-padas have been spoken!' Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these words: Whoever, Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, aspires to the <s>bodhisattva</s> stages, wealth, grain, enjoyments, sovereignty, kingship, the status of a <s>vidyādhara</s> (knowledge-holder), longevity, strength, vigor, and long life — that person should, on the bright eighth day, make an image of <s>Vajradhara</s> out of white sandalwood, laughing loudly, adorned with all ornaments. A heart-shrine containing relics should be made. The <s>Vajradhara</s> with relics, the reassuring <s>vidyādhara</s>, should be [worshipped] with incense burning, by one who is pure and has fasted day and night. Then on the eighth day, having performed the preliminary consecration

body.text: kṛtvā śuce satathāgatasthāne mahatā dhūpapuṣpagandhadīpaiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā triskṛtvā aṣṭaśatiko jāpo dātavyaḥ tathāgatasya pūjā kartavyā / sarvatathāgatānāṃ namaskṛtya catvāri pūrṇakumbhā[ni]sthāpya raktacandanamayaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā śvetavastrāprāvṛtena ekāgramānasena caturdiśe ca rasagandhamadyapāyasavaliṃ dattvā aṣṭaśatasumanaḥpuṣpaiḥ vajrapāṇirāhartavyaḥ / yāvat pañcadaśī tato mahānirghoṣo bhaviṣyati pṛthivīkampaśca raśmayo niścariṣyanti / tato yathepsitaṃ varaṃ dāsyāmi / sarvakarmāṇi sarvakāryāṇi japitamātreṇa samṛddhiṣyanti / vigatavyādhayo cirajīvī sarvapāpavivarjito bhaviṣyati / guṇasahasraṃ pratilapsyate / maraṇakāle ca buddhaṃ paśyati / ahaṃ ca darśanaṃ dāsyāmi / atha bhagavān sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu vajrapāṇe anatikramaṇīyā iyaṃ mudrā / nātra kāṃkṣā na vimatirna vicikitsā kartavyā sadevakena lokena /
body.translated_text: in a pure place where a <s>Tathāgata</s> [image] is established, having performed worship with great offerings of incense, flowers, fragrances, and lamps, the recitation of eight hundred [mantras] should be performed three times, and worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> should be done. Having bowed to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having set up four full vessels, having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> of red sandalwood, covered with white cloth, with a one-pointed mind, having offered oblations of essences, fragrances, liquor, and rice-milk in the four directions, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> should be invoked with eight hundred jasmine flowers. Until the fifteenth day, then there will be a great thundering sound, the earth will tremble, and rays of light will shine forth. Then I will grant the desired boon. All actions and all endeavors will be accomplished merely by recitation. One will be free from diseases, long-lived, and rid of all sins. One will obtain a thousand virtues. At the time of death, one will see the <s>Buddha</s>. And I too will grant a vision [of myself]. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave his approval: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>! This seal is inviolable. No doubt, no hesitation, no uncertainty should be entertained [regarding it] by the world including the gods.'

body.text: III
body.translated_text: III

body.text: atha maṃjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocat / kenārthenāyaṃ bhagavan sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānasattvāvalokanabuddhakṣetrasandarśanavyūho nāma samādhirucyate / bhagavānāha / sarvatathāgatānāmadhiṣṭhānaṃ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these words: For what reason, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is this <s>samādhi</s> called 'the Array of Empowerment by All <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Observation of Beings, and Display of <s>Buddha</s>-Fields'? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: The empowerment of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>

body.text: sarvabodhisattvānām adhiṣṭhitaśca sarvasamādhiṃ sarvadhāraṇīmukhāni pratilabhate / sarvasattvānāṃ cittacaitasikasamiṃjitaprasāritāni prajānāti / devānāṃ nāgānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ yakṣāṇāṃ gandharvāṇāṃ pretānāṃ tiryagyonigatānāṃ yāmalaukikānām amī sattvāḥ puṇyopagāḥ sukṛtakarā buddhadharmasaṃgheṣu prasādaṃ pratilabhante / amī narakagāmiduṣkṛtagāmipāpakāriṇaḥ / teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ pāpadṛṣṭigatānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati sarvapāpebhyo nivārayati / buddhabodhau pratiṣṭhāpayati sarvābhiprāyaṃ paripūrayati / īrṣyāmānakrodhamātsaryaṃ vinodayati / te ca sattvā buddhadharmasaṃgheṣu prasādaṃ pratilabhya buddhakṣetreṣupapadyante / na jātu duḥkhamanubhavanti na daurmanasyam / tenāyaṃ kulaputra sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānasattvāvalokanabuddhakṣetrasandarśanavyūho nāma samādhirucyate / yaṃ śrutvā niyatāvaivarthikabhūmiṃ pratilabhante /
body.translated_text: and the empowerment of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> — one attains all <s>samādhis</s> and all <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gates. One knows the mental and mental-factor activities — the contracting and extending — of all beings: of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, humans, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, beings in animal realms, and those in <s>Yama</s>'s world. [One sees that] these beings are endowed with merit, doers of good deeds — they gain faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>. [And one sees that] those are destined for hell, destined for evil rebirths, doers of evil. To those beings who have gone to evil views, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> and turns them away from all evil. He establishes them in the awakening of the <s>Buddha</s> and fulfills all their aspirations. He dispels jealousy, pride, anger, and miserliness. And those beings, having gained faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>, are reborn in <s>Buddha</s>-fields. They never experience suffering or dejection. Therefore, O son of good family, this <s>samādhi</s> is called 'the Array of Empowerment by All <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Observation of Beings, and Display of <s>Buddha</s>-Fields.' Having heard it, they certainly attain the irreversible stage.

body.text: sa
body.translated_text: He said: For what reason, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does the prophecy (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) for those sons of good family come about? How great is their mass of merit? What is the difficult practice? Is <s>arhatship</s> difficult, <s>Bhagavān</s>, let alone unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: O son of good family, by me, from the first generation of the aspiration for awakening (<s>prathamacittotpāda</s>), the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) of giving (<s>dāna</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) were fulfilled, and the sacrifice of head, hands, feet, eyes, the best part of the body, dear sons, wives, daughters, male and female servants was made, and whoever [were to compare that merit with the merit]

body.text: āha / kenārthena bhagavaṃsteṣāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ vyākaraṇaṃ bhavati / kiyatteṣāṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ bhavati / kiṃ duṣkaracaryā / duṣkaraṃ ca bhagavan arhattvaṃ prāgevānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ / bhagavānāha / yaśca mayā kulaputra prathamacittotpādamupādāya dānaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñāpāramitā paripūritā yaśca śiraḥkara caraṇanayanottamāṃgapriyaputrabhāryāduhitṛdāsadāsīparityāga kṛtaḥ yaścāsya dharmaparyāyasya
body.translated_text: of this <s>Dharma</s> discourse

body.text: pūjanasatkaraṇalikhanalekhāpanavācanodgrahaṇīyaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ parebhyaḥ saṃprakāśanīyaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ teṣāṃ ca dharmabhāṇakānāṃ pūjanasatkaraṇapuṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ tasyāyaṃ pūrvimakaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ śatatamāmapi kalāṃ nopaiti / yaśca mayā kulaputra dharmo bhāṣitaḥ paryāvāptaḥ taṃ sarvaṃ satkare gurukare mānaye pūjaye satkṛtya likhaye likhāpaye / yaścāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ likhe vācaye pūjaye saṃprakāśaye bahutaram itaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraṃ parigrahīṣyati / tatastathāgato vyākarotyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / tat kasya hetoḥ / evaṃrūpasya duṣkaraṃ dharmaparyāyasya śravaṇodgrahaṇadhāraṇapūjanalikhanam / te ca sattvāḥ pāpasamācārāḥ khādyapeyahāsyanāṭyābhiratā aśubhe śubhasaṃjñinaḥ kāmakrodhavyāpādabahulā asukhe sukhasaṃjñinaḥ prahārākrośatarjanatāḍanābhiratā na jñāsyanti na manasi kariṣyanti / te tataḥ pāpakarmanidānājñānā akalyāṇamitraparigṛhītā jarāvyādhiśokamṛtyuparipīḍitā maraṇakāle paritarpyante / śmaśānasadṛśamaṃcāvalaṃvyamānaṃ parasparaṃ paśyanti na ca kuśalacittamutpādayiṣyanti nābhedyaprasādam / te tataścyavitvā punarapi duḥkhāni pratyanubhaviṣyanti / nāyaṃ kulaputrākṛtakuśalamūlaistathāgatādarśāvino
body.translated_text: worship, honoring, writing, copying, reading, and memorizing — this is the meritorious preparation; it should be made known to others — this is the meritorious preparation; and the meritorious preparation of worshipping and honoring those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers — the former meritorious preparation does not reach even a hundredth part of this. And whatever <s>Dharma</s> I have spoken and mastered, noble son — all of that I honor, revere, esteem, and worship, and I write and cause to be written. And whoever writes, reads, worships, and proclaims this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse will accumulate even more meritorious preparation than this. Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> gives prophecy of unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). For what reason? Because the hearing, memorizing, retaining, worshipping, and writing of such a difficult <s>Dharma</s>-discourse is a difficult deed. Those beings who are of evil conduct, delighting in food, drink, laughter, and theater, perceiving the impure as pure, full of desire, anger, and malice, perceiving the unhappy as happy, delighting in striking, reviling, threatening, and beating — they will neither understand nor take it to heart. Then, due to the cause of evil deeds, seized by ignorance and evil companions, tormented by old age, disease, sorrow, and death, at the time of death they are [vainly] satisfied. Seeing one another mounted on biers resembling funeral grounds, they will neither generate a wholesome thought nor unbreakable faith. Then, having fallen from there, they will again experience sufferings. This, noble son, cannot be heard, honored, worshipped, memorized, or written by those with uncultivated roots of merit, who have not seen the <s>Tathāgata</s>,

body.text: avyākaraṇaprāptaiḥ śrotuṃ mānayituṃ pūjayitum udgrahītuṃ na likhituṃ na likhāpayituṃ na śraddhadhātuṃ na ca tān dharmabhāṇakān satkartuṃ mānayituṃ pūjayitum [api na śakyate /] tathāgatakṛtyaṃ kulaputra tatra viṣaye bhaviṣyati yatrāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ pracariṣyati / atha sā yathā samāgatā parṣat sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu bhagavan / vayamapi bhagavan dharmabhāṇakaṃ dharmaśrāvaṇikaṃ tathāgatakṛtyena satkariṣyāmaḥ gurūkariṣyāmaḥ mānayiṣyāmaḥ sarvasukhopadhānaṃ cāsyopasaṃhariṣyāmaḥ / ayaṃ ca dharmaparyāyaṃ vaistarikīkariṣyāmaḥ rakṣiṣyāmaḥ yenāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaściraśtitiko bhaviṣyati / atha bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ yathā samāgatāṃ parṣadamavalokyaivamāhuḥ / sādhu sādhu kulaputra / aho evamapi yuṣmākaṃ karaṇīyam / kāyacittanirapekṣairbhūtvā sarvopaplavanaparibhavanaparibhāṣaṇatarjanaprahārākrośalabhyamānam [api] imaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ śrāvayitavyo likhitavyo vācayitavyaḥ / taṃ ca dharmabhāṇakaṃ dharmaśrāvaṇikaṃ sarvasukhopadhānena copasthātavyaḥ / sa ca viṣayaḥ sa ca dvīpaḥ sa ca nagaro rakṣitavyaḥ sarvabhayopadravopasargopāyāsebhyaḥ / tasya ca kulaputrasya kuladuhiturvā satatasamitaṃ samanvāhartavyam / atha bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata /
body.translated_text: who have not obtained prophecy — they are unable to hear, honor, worship, memorize, write, cause to be written, have faith in, or honor, esteem, and worship those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers. The work of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, noble son, will be in that region where this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse will circulate. Then the assembly that had gathered gave its approval: Excellent! Excellent, <s>Bhagavān</s>! We too, <s>Bhagavān</s>, will honor, revere, and esteem the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher and the <s>Dharma</s>-listener as the work of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and we will provide them with all comforts. And we will make this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse widespread and will protect it, so that this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse may endure for a long time. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that time, looking upon the assembled gathering, spoke thus: Excellent! Excellent, noble sons! Indeed, this is what should be done by you — becoming heedless of body and mind, this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse should be taught, written, and recited, even when one encounters all manner of calamities, contempt, reproach, threats, beatings, and abuse. And that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher and <s>Dharma</s>-listener should be attended to with all comforts. And that region, that island, and that city should be protected from all fears, dangers, afflictions, and disturbances. And that noble son or noble daughter should be constantly attended to. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: śṛṇuta kulaputra apramattā mā paścakāle parittāpyu bheṣyatha /
children.translated_text: Listen, noble sons, with diligence — do not later have regret!

children.text: buddhasya utpādyu kadāci labhyate kalpānakoṭībhi śataiḥ sahasraiḥ //
children.translated_text: The arising of a <s>Buddha</s> is rarely obtained, even in <s>koṭis</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>.

children.text: guṇāśca śṛṇvatvabhiśraddadheta na durlabhā teṣu samādhi bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: Hearing the virtues, one should have faith — for them, <s>samādhi</s> will not be difficult to attain.

children.text: kalpānakoṭīn yatha gaṅgavālikā yo dānu dadyā dvipadottameṣu //
children.translated_text: As for one who, for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, would give gifts to the best among bipeds —

children.text: dhanaṃ cā dhānyaṃ tatha vastrabhūṣaṇaṃ gandhaṃ ca mālyaṃ ca vilepanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: wealth and grain, and likewise garments, ornaments, incense, garlands, and ointments —

children.text: yaścaiva sutramabhiśraddadhitvā śruṇeya vāceya likhāpayeta /
children.translated_text: and one who, having placed faith in this <s>sūtra</s>, would hear it, recite it, and cause it to be written —

children.text: na tasya puṇyasya pramāṇu vidyate tā cāpramāṇaṃ sugatena deśitam //
children.translated_text: the measure of that merit cannot be known, for it has been taught by the <s>Sugata</s> to be immeasurable.

children.text: raṇyaṃ ca seveta sadāpramatto dhyānaṃ ca dhyāyetu sadānyacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should frequent the forest, ever diligent, and meditate constantly with a focused mind.

children.text: dānaṃ ca dadyā priyaputradhītarā hastau ca pādau ca parityajeta //
children.translated_text: One may give in charity one's beloved sons and daughters, and relinquish one's hands and feet —

children.text: yathaiva sūtrasya dhareti kaści ayaṃ tato puṇyaviśeṣyu prāpnuyā /
children.translated_text: yet whoever holds this <s>sūtra</s> will obtain a greater distinction of merit than that.

children.text: arthasya dātā varasūtrametat sarvasyāpāyā sadā varjitāsya //
children.translated_text: The giver of this supreme <s>sūtra</s>'s meaning is forever freed from all lower rebirths.

children.text: dhanasya dhānyasya ca dāyako hyayaṃ guṇāśca sarve 'pi na tasya durlabhāḥ /
children.translated_text: This giver of wealth and grain — all virtues are not difficult for him to obtain.

children.text: āyurbalaṃ vīryu na tasya durlabhaṃ dhāreti sūtraṃ ya imaṃ viśuddham //
children.translated_text: Long life, strength, and vigor are not difficult for one who holds this pure <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: drakṣyanti buddhamamitābhu nāyakaṃ mayāpi sa vyākṛtu buddhabodhau /
children.translated_text: They will see <s>Buddha</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, the Guide, and they will also be prophesied by me for <s>Buddha</s>-awakening.

children.text: na tasya pāpaṃ pi kadāci vidyate sukhāvatīṃ drakṣyati lokadhātum //
children.translated_text: Not even a trace of evil will exist for them — they will see the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>.

children.text: yaṃ cāpi tasya sada karmu bheṣyati sarvaṃ kṣayaṃ yāsyati cittanīḍe /
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>karma</s> remains for them, all of it will be exhausted in the nest of the mind.

children.text: kāyasya śūle tatha śīrṣatāpe na tasya jātu vinipātu bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: In bodily pain or headache, never will there be downfall for them.

children.text: sāṃdṛṣṭikāṃścāpi guṇāṃ sa lapsyate sarvaṃ yathā cintitu prārthitaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: They will also obtain visible qualities in this very life, and all that they think and wish for will be fulfilled.

children.text: tasmābhi tebhi sada bhikṣubhikṣuṇī upāsakopāsika rājabhiḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, always by those <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, <s>upāsikās</s>, and kings —

children.text: gurugauravaṃ kṛtvā ca dharmabhāṇake yathā narendrasya tathāgatasya //
children.translated_text: having shown great respect to the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, just as to the Lord of Men, the <s>Tathāgata</s> —

children.text: idaṃ ca sūtraṃ sada dhāritavyaṃ satkāru nityaṃ ca kartavyadhārake /
children.translated_text: this <s>sūtra</s> should always be upheld, and constant honor should be shown to the one who holds it.

children.text: gandhaiśca mālyaiśca vilepanaiśca satkāru kṛtvā ca likhāpayeta //
children.translated_text: With incense, garlands, and ointments, having shown honor, one should cause it to be written.

children.text: mā paścakāle jaravyādhipīḍitā aneka-āyāsasahasravyākulāḥ /
children.translated_text: Lest in the final age, tormented by old age and disease, beset by thousands of manifold troubles,

children.text: narakeṣu tiryakṣu paribhramāṇāḥ ṣaṇḍhāśca paṇḍāśca jugupsanīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: wandering in hells and animal realms, becoming eunuchs, impotent, and contemptible,

children.text: jātyandhabhūtāḥ kuṇapāśca gandhinaḥ saṃjāsyate nīcakuleṣu strīṣu //
children.translated_text: born blind, corpse-like and foul-smelling — they be born among women in low families.

children.text: īrṣyālukasya sada pāpacāriṇaḥ krodhābhibhūtasya ca matsariṣya /
children.translated_text: For the ever-jealous, the evildoer, the one overcome by anger and envy —

children.text: buddheṣu dharmeṣu karitva gauravam imeṣu jātīṣūpapadyate 'sau /
children.translated_text: having shown no reverence to the <s>Buddhas</s> and the <s>Dharma</s> — one is reborn in such births.

children.text: tatraiva duḥkhāni ca vedamānā mā paścakāle paritāpyu bheṣyatha //
children.translated_text: There, experiencing those sufferings — do not later have regret!

children.text: tasmābhi tehi sada pūjitasya yaścaiva dhāreta prakāśayeta /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by those who always worship [this <s>sūtra</s>], whoever upholds and proclaims it —

children.text: yaścaiva paribhāṣaṇu tasya kurvate jugupsanāṃ tāḍanabandhanañca //
children.translated_text: and whoever subjects them to reproach, abuse, beating, and imprisonment —

children.text: mamaiva tena paribhāṣaṇā kṛtā mamaiva satkāru karitva dhārake /
children.translated_text: it is as if the reproach were done to me myself; and it is as if honor were shown to me through the one who holds it.

children.text: tasmācca tairhi sada dharmabhāṇake yaścaiva dhāreta likheta vācaye /
children.translated_text: Therefore, always to the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher — whoever upholds, writes, or recites it —

children.text: satkāru taiśca sad anityu kuryā srigdhāśca vāco madhurā bhaṇeta //
children.translated_text: honor should always be shown by them, and affectionate and sweet words should be spoken.

body.text: IV
body.translated_text: IV

body.text: āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo bhagavataścaraṇayornipatya bhagavantametadavocat / anusmarāmyahaṃ bhagavan asti vyavalokanaprātihāryā nāma dhāraṇī yā mayā pūrvaṃ jñānaketuprabhākarasya tathāgatasyāntikādudgṛhītā śrutā[ca] / yāṃ śrutvā matvā udgṛhya dhārayitvā vācayitvā satkaritvā likhitvā likhāpayitvā avaivartikabhūmiṃ pratilabhante / sarvānetāṃstathāgatabhāṣitān guṇān pratilabhante / sarvaṃ cāsya yathābhiprāyāṃ samṛdhyate / sarvakarmāva[ra]ṇaṃ cāsya kṣayaṃ gacchati / samādhiṃ ca pratilabhate / vigatā vyādhayo bhavanti / buddhadarśanaṃ bodhisattvadarśanaṃ bhavati / tad bhagavān sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu kulaputra pravartaya adhiṣṭhitaṃ tathāgatena /
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, prostrating at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these words: I recall, <s>Bhagavān</s>, there is a <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Vyavalokana-prātihāryā</s> (the Miracle of Gazing) which I formerly received and heard from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jñānaketuprabhākara</s>. Having heard it, understood it, memorized it, retained it, recited it, honored it, written it, and caused it to be written, one attains the irreversible stage (<s>avaivartika-bhūmi</s>). One obtains all these virtues spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. All one's wishes are fulfilled. All one's <s>karmāvaraṇa</s> (karmic obscurations) are exhausted. One attains <s>samādhi</s>. Diseases are removed. One beholds <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> gave his approval: Excellent! Excellent, noble son! Proceed — it is empowered by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: athāryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo daśadiśaṃ sarvatathāgatebhyo namaskṛtya imāni mantrapadāni bhāṣate sma /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, having paid homage to all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions, spoke these <s>mantra</s>-words:

body.text: namaḥ sarvatathāgatānāṃ sarvāśāparipūrakarāṇām / nama āryāvalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahākāruṇikasya / tadyathā
body.translated_text: Homage to all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the fulfillers of all wishes! Homage to the <s>bodhisattva</s> Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the greatly compassionate one! <s>Tadyathā</s> —

body.text: ha ha ha ha / mama mama / dhiri dhiri / śānte praśānte sarvapāpakṣayaṃkare / avalokaya kāruṇika bodhicittaṃ manasi kuru / vyavalokaya māṃ smara smara yat tvayā pūrvaṃ satyādhiṣṭhānaṃ kṛtam / tena satyena sarvāśāṃ me paripūraya / buddhakṣetraṃ pariśodhaya / mā me kaścid viheṭhaṃ karotu / buddhādhiṣṭhānena svāhā / tadyathā
body.translated_text: <s>Ha ha ha ha / mama mama / dhiri dhiri / śānte praśānte sarvapāpakṣayaṃkare</s> — O peaceful one, O most peaceful one, O destroyer of all evil! — <s>avalokaya kāruṇika bodhicittaṃ manasi kuru</s> — Gaze [upon us], O compassionate one, generate the mind of awakening! — <s>vyavalokaya māṃ smara smara yat tvayā pūrvaṃ satyādhiṣṭhānaṃ kṛtam</s> — Look upon me, remember, remember the vow of truth you formerly made! — <s>tena satyena sarvāśāṃ me paripūraya</s> — By that truth, fulfill all my wishes! — <s>buddhakṣetraṃ pariśodhaya</s> — Purify the <s>Buddha</s>-field! — <s>mā me kaścid viheṭhaṃ karotu</s> — Let no one cause me harm! — <s>buddhādhiṣṭhānena svāhā</s> — By the empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! — <s>Tadyathā</s> —

body.text: teje teje mahāteje / yanmama kāyaduścaritaṃ vāgduścaritaṃ manoduścaritaṃ dāridrayaṃ vā tanme kṣapaya / ālokaya vilokaya / tathāgatadarśanaṃ cāhamabhikāṃkṣāmi bodhisattvadarśanam / dhudhupa dadasva me darśanam / sarve me kuśalā abhivardhantu / namaḥ sarvatathāgatānām / namaḥ avalokiteśvarasya / smara pratijñā mahāsattvāḥ / sidhyantu mantrapadāḥ svāhā /
body.translated_text: Splendor, splendor, great splendor! Whatever bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, or poverty I have — destroy that for me! Look upon me, gaze upon me! I desire the vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and the vision of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. <s>Dhudhupa</s>, grant me a vision! May all my merits increase! Homage to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>! Homage to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>! Remember your vow, O <s>Mahāsattvas</s> (great beings)! May the <s>mantra</s>-words be accomplished, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: asyāṃ dhāraṇyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ mahāpṛthivīkaṃpo 'bhūt mahākilakilāśabdaḥ / divyaṃ ca puṣpavarṣamabhipravarṣan[sarvaḥ saparṣat] sādhukārasmadāt / sādhu sādhu subhāṣitamidaṃ mahāsattvena sarvasattvānāṃ trāṇārthaṃ sarvāśāparipūrakaram / rakṣa sarvabhayebhyaḥ sarvakarmakṣayaṃkara maraṇaduḥsvapnakāntārapraśamana / vayamapi sarve bhūtvā dhārayiṣyāmaḥ satkariṣyāmaḥ / avalokiteśvara āha / yaḥ kaścit kulaputra imān guṇānabhikāṃkṣa[te] / yathā tathāgatena parikirtitaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ mama kāṃkṣa[te] / mamāpi sammukhadarśanaṃ samādhilambhaṃ buddhabodhisattvadarśanaṃ
body.translated_text: When this <s>dhāraṇī</s> was being spoken, a great earthquake occurred along with a great sound of jubilation. A divine rain of flowers showered down, and the entire assembly uttered exclamations of approval: 'Excellent, excellent! Well spoken by the <s>mahāsattva</s> (great being), for the protection of all beings, fulfilling all wishes — protecting from all fears, causing the destruction of all <s>karma</s>, pacifying death, bad dreams, and dangers. We too shall all uphold and honor [this <s>dhāraṇī</s>].' <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> said: 'Whatever son of good family desires these qualities — desires the prophecy proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> concerning me, and desires face-to-face vision of me, attainment of <s>samādhi</s>, vision of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,

body.text: bhogaiśvaryalambhaṃ buddhakṣetropapattiṃ tena śuklapakṣe śucinā susnātagātreṇa bhūtvā āryāṣṭāṃgopavāsopavasitairaṣṭamyāmārabhya śucau pradeśe buddhādhiṣṭhite gandhapuṣpairdhvajapatākaiḥ pūrṇakumbhairabhyarcya sa pṛthivīpradeśaḥ sa ca dharmabhāṇakaḥ śuciḥ susnātagātraḥ śvetavastraprāvṛto nānāpuṣpamālyagandhairabhyarcya likhāpayitavyaḥ sarvasattvāsādhāraṇāni kuśalamūlāni kṛtvā sarvasattvamaitracittena dayācittena karuṇācittena tathāgatagurugauravaṃ cittamupasthāpya tena dine dine likhatā tāva likhe yāvadardhadivasam / aṣṭamyāmārabhya yāvat pañcadaśīṃ dine dine saiva pūjā kartavyā / tato 'nenaiva vidhinā likhitamātreṇa pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi sarvapāpāni cāsya kṣayaṃ yāsyanti / kuśalairdharmairvivardhiṣyate / uttaptavīryo bhaviṣyati / sarvadharmeṣu kāyasukhamanuprāpsyati / tanūbhaviṣyanti rāgadveṣamohamānakrodhāḥ / tena likhāpayitvā pūrvamukhīṃ sadhātukāṃ tathāgatapratimāmavalokiteśvarapratimāṃ ca sadhātukāṃ sthāpya sadhātukeai caitāyatane puṣpadhūpagandhairdīpaiśca udāratarā pūjā kartavyā / aṣṭamyāmārabhya yāvat pañcadaśīṃ sarvasattvamahākaruṇācittena bhavitavyam / śuciśuklabhojinā āryāṣṭāṃgopavāsopavasitena suhṛtsahāyakena mānakrodhamātsaryaparivarjitena dine dine udāratarāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā trisandhyaṃ jāpaḥ aṣṭaśatiko dātavyaḥ / dīpadhūpapuṣpagandhādi dattvā sumanaḥpuṣpāṣṭaśataiśca āryāvalokiteśvarapratimā trisandhyamāhartavyā /
body.translated_text: attainment of enjoyments and sovereignty, and rebirth in a <s>Buddha</s>-field — that person, during the bright fortnight, being clean with a well-bathed body, having observed the noble eightfold fast (<s>āryāṣṭāṅga-upavāsa</s>), beginning from the eighth day, in a clean place blessed by the <s>Buddha</s>, having worshipped with incense, flowers, banners, flags, and full water-pots, [should prepare] that spot of earth. The <s>Dharma</s>-preacher too, clean, with bathed body, covered with white garments, having worshipped with various flowers, garlands, and incense, should have [this <s>dhāraṇī</s>] written. Having performed roots of merit uncommon to all beings, with a mind of friendliness, compassion, and mercy toward all beings, having generated a mind of reverence for the <s>Tathāgata</s> as teacher — he should write daily, writing until midday. From the eighth to the fifteenth day, the same worship should be performed daily. Then, merely by writing according to this method, the five heinous acts (<s>pañcānantarya karmas</s>) and all sins will be destroyed. He will increase in meritorious qualities. He will become of intense vigor. He will attain bodily comfort in all <s>dharmas</s>. Passion, hatred, delusion, pride, and anger will become diminished. Having had [this] written, he should set up an east-facing <s>Tathāgata</s> image with relics and an <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> image with relics, and at a <s>caitya</s>-shrine with relics, a most excellent worship should be performed with flowers, incense, fragrances, and lamps. From the eighth to the fifteenth day, one should abide with a mind of great compassion for all beings. Eating pure and white food, having observed the noble eightfold fast, with a well-wishing companion, free from pride, anger, and jealousy, performing a most excellent worship daily, the <s>japa</s> (recitation) of eight hundred should be given three times daily. Having offered lamps, incense, flowers, and fragrances, the image of Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> should be honored three times daily with eight hundred <s>sumanas</s> (jasmine) flowers.

body.text: vajrapāṇeśca dhūpo dātavyaḥ / daśadiśamabhinamaskṛtya paścimena bhīmāyā devyāḥ pūrveṇānopamāyāḥ ūrdhvena śaṃkhinyā balirnānārasapāyasadadhyodanaścaturdiśaṃ kṣeptavyaḥ / tatastasya na kaścid vikṣepaṃ kariṣyati / saṃtrāso ['pi notpadyate /] nānyathātvaṃ cittasya / sarveṣāṃ cāṣṭaśatiko jāpaḥ aṣṭaśatasumanaḥpuṣpaiśca saṃcodanam / [ane]naiva vidhinā pūrvasecaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ pūrṇapañcadaśyāṃ catvāri pūrṇakuṃbhā[ni]sthāpya dhūpacandanakundurukakarpūraṃ dattvā dīpa[mukhāni] catvāri nānāgandhadhvajapaṭapatākāsuvarṇarūpyabhāṇḍaiḥ taṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ samalaṃkṛtya dadhimadhupāyasadadhyodanamanyāni ca yathālambhena baliṃ caturdiśe dattvā nivedya sumanaḥpuṣpāṣṭakaśatairekaikaṃ japya caturdiśe kṣeptavyam / pūrvavat tryaṣṭaśataiḥ sumanojātipuṣpairekaikaṃ japya āryāvalokiteśvarapratimā āhartavyā / tataḥ satpratimā kaṃpiṣyati / mahānirghoṣo bhaviṣyati / raśmayo niścariṣyanti / pṛthivīkampaḥ [bhaviṣyati /] tataḥ sarvakarmāṇi sarvakāryāṇi cāsya samṛddhiṣyanti / tathāgatadarśanaṃ bodhisattvabhūmipratilambhaḥ sarvasattvavandanīyo bhaviṣyati / dhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgārasamṛddhaḥ sarvavyādhiparivarjitaścirajīvi
body.translated_text: Incense should be offered to <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>. Having paid homage to the ten directions, a <s>bali</s> (offering) of various flavored rice-pudding and curd-rice should be cast in four directions — on the west for the goddess <s>Bhīmā</s>, on the east for <s>Anopamā</s>, and above for <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>. Then no one will cause disturbance to him. No fear will arise. There will be no alteration of mind. For all of them, a recitation of eight hundred and invocation with eight hundred <s>sumanas</s> flowers [should be performed]. Having performed the preliminary consecration according to this very method, then on the full fifteenth day, having set up four full water-pots, having offered incense of sandalwood, <s>kunduruka</s> (frankincense), and camphor, and four lamp-faces, having adorned that spot of earth with various fragrant banners, cloths, flags, and vessels of gold and silver, having given offerings of curd, honey, rice-pudding, and curd-rice and other things as available in the four directions, having announced [to the deities], and having recited over each [offering] with eight hundred <s>sumanas</s> flowers, they should be cast in the four directions. As before, with three times eight hundred <s>sumanā</s> and <s>jātī</s> (jasmine) flowers, having recited over each, the image of Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> should be honored. Then the noble image will tremble. A great sound will arise. Rays of light will emanate. An earthquake will occur. Then all his <s>karmas</s> and all his endeavors will be fulfilled. He will gain the vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, attainment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages, and will become worthy of worship by all beings. He will be prosperous with wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses, free from all diseases, and long-lived.

body.text: [bhaviṣyati] / sarvaśatravaḥ sarvarājarājaputrāmātyadarśanābhikāṃkṣiṇo bhaviṣyanti priyaṃkarāḥ sarvakleśarāgadveṣamohaprahīṇāḥ / na ca jātu priyaviprayogo bhaviṣyati / mahādṛḍhabalavīryasaṃpannastejavāṃstīkṣṇendriyo buddhimān sarvasattvadayācitto dharmajño yāvaccyavanakāle buddhaṃ bhagavantamāryāvalokiteśvaraṃ paśyati / maitravihārī kālaṃ karoti / dharmaṃ deśayamānaṃ yathepsiteṣu buddhakṣetreṣu mahācakravartikuleṣu yatrānusmṛtiṃ karoti tatropapadyate / anyāni cānekāni guṇasahasrāṇi pratilapsyate / evaṃ bhagavan bahuguṇakaro 'yaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ / imāni te dhāraṇīmantrapadāni na vinā tathāgatādhiṣṭhānasyāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śakyaṃ śrotuṃ na dhārayituṃ na pūjayituṃ na likhituṃ na likhāyituṃ na śraddadhātum / sace darśanaṃ bhave na śravaṃ bhaviṣyati / sace śravaṇaṃ tadvikṣiptacittaḥ śroṣyati na śraddhāsyati na satkariṣyati / sace satkare kleśavyāpādacittaḥ[satkariṣyati] sace likhe likhāpayeta vyākṣiptacittaḥ / [tat kasya hetoḥ] / tathā hi tasya pūrvapāpakarmaphalahetutvāt karmānubhavitavyam / sa vicikitsāprāpto bhaviṣyati / paṃcānantaryaṃ kariṣyati / tribhiḥ sādhanaiḥ sarvāśāsamṛddhirbhaviṣyati / nātra kāṃkṣā na vimatirna vicikitsotpādayitavyā / atha bhagavān[avalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya] sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu kulaputra / tathāgatakṛtyamayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ kariṣyati sarvasattvānām /
body.translated_text: [He will be long-lived.] All enemies, all kings, princes, and ministers will desire to see him, and will be favorable toward him. He will have abandoned all afflictions — passion, hatred, and delusion. There will never be separation from loved ones. Endowed with great firmness, strength, and vigor, he will be radiant, sharp-sensed, intelligent, compassionate toward all beings, and a knower of <s>Dharma</s>. At the time of death, he will behold the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s> and Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>. He will die abiding in friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>). While teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, he will be reborn in whichever <s>Buddha</s>-fields and great <s>Cakravartin</s> families he recollects and wishes for. He will also obtain many other thousands of virtues. Thus, <s>Bhagavān</s>, this <s>Dharma</s> discourse (<s>dharmaparyāya</s>) produces many virtues. These <s>dhāraṇī mantra</s>-words — without the empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, this <s>Dharma</s> discourse cannot be heard, nor upheld, nor worshipped, nor written, nor caused to be written, nor believed. If there is seeing, there will be no hearing. If there is hearing, one will hear with a distracted mind and will not believe, will not honor [it]. If one honors [it], one will honor with a mind of defilement and malice. If one writes or causes [it] to be written, [one will do so] with a distracted mind. What is the reason? Because, due to the fruit of that person's prior evil <s>karma</s>, the <s>karma</s> must be experienced. That person will become afflicted by doubt. He will commit the five heinous acts (<s>pañcānantarya</s>). By the three means of accomplishment, all wishes will be fulfilled. Herein, no uncertainty, no disagreement, no doubt should be generated.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave his exclamation of approval to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, son of good family! This <s>Dharma</s> discourse will accomplish the work of the <s>Tathāgata</s> for all beings.'

body.text: V
body.translated_text: V

body.text: atha khalvanopamā mahāyakṣiṇī yena bhagavāṃstenopasamakrāmat / bhagavantaṃ nānāpuṣpaduṣyayugairācchādya bhagavataḥ pādayornipatya bhagavantametadavocat / evaṃ smarāmyahaṃ bhagavanmayā bhagavataḥ kauśāmbyāṃ ghoṣilasyārāme viharataḥ purataḥ pratijñā samudāhṛtā sarvasattvānāmarthāya / ahamapi bhagavan sarvavidyādharāṇāṃ hṛdayaṃ jānāmi / tanme bhagavānanujānātu bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya sarvāśāparipūraṇārthāya bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikānāṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>yakṣiṇī</s> <s>Anopamā</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having covered the <s>Bhagavān</s> with various flower-garlands and pairs of garments, having prostrated at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, she addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these words: 'Thus do I remember, <s>Bhagavān</s> — by me, in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s> while dwelling in <s>Ghoṣila</s>'s park at <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, a vow was uttered for the benefit of all beings. I too, <s>Bhagavān</s>, know the heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>) of all <s>vidyādhara</s> (knowledge-holder) [spells]. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> grant me permission, for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, for the fulfillment of all wishes, and for <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, and <s>upāsikās</s>.'

body.text: namaḥ sarvatathāgatānāṃ saṃyyathīd ha ha / hī hī / hu hu / sara sara / lahuṃ lahuṃ / śīghraṃ śīghraṃ / mahāvidye sarvavidyādharanamaskṛte / hasaḥ hasaḥ / kiṃ tiṣṭhasi kiṃ tiṣṭhasi / kanakavicitrābharaṇavibhūṣitāṃgi paṭa paṭa / bhara bhara / bhiri bhiri / bhūru bhūru / sarvārthaṃ me sādhaya / turu turu / arthaṃ sādhaya / arthaṃ dehi me
body.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>! <s>Saṃyathīdaṃ</s>: <s>ha ha</s>! <s>hī hī</s>! <s>hu hu</s>! <s>sara sara</s>! <s>lahuṃ lahuṃ</s>! Quickly, quickly! O great <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge-spell), saluted by all <s>vidyādharas</s> (knowledge-holders)! <s>hasaḥ hasaḥ</s>! Why do you stand? Why do you stand? O one adorned with ornaments of variegated gold! Read, read! Bear, bear! <s>bhiri bhiri</s>! <s>bhūru bhūru</s>! Accomplish all purposes for me! <s>turu turu</s>! Accomplish the purpose! Give me the purpose!

body.text: nātsahaṃ mārapati śūlkṣiṇasya /
body.translated_text: I cannot endure [the power of] <s>Mārapati</s> (the lord of Māra), the spear-bearer.

body.text: sarvasaṅghānāḥ
body.translated_text: May there be

body.text: siddhiṃ hā hā / padme padme mahāpadme / viśade viśade mahāviśade / bhava bhava bhavodbhavāya / tamahaṃ ghore tamahaṃ ghore /
body.translated_text: accomplishment for all <s>saṅghas</s>! <s>hā hā</s>! <s>Padme padme mahāpadme</s> (O lotus, lotus, great lotus)! <s>Viśade viśade mahāviśade</s> (O pure one, pure one, greatly pure one)! Become, become, for the arising of existence! I [dispel] the terrible darkness, I [dispel] the terrible darkness!

body.text: tanme vidyāṃ prayojaya / siddhiṃ kuru / sarvaśāṃ me paripūraya buddhādhiṣṭhānena svāhā /
body.translated_text: Employ that <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge-spell) for me! Bring about accomplishment! Fulfill all my wishes, by the empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: yaḥ kaścidbhagavadguṇārthī dhanadhānyārthī sarvasattvavaśīkaraṇārthī bhave mahaiśvaryaṃ rājatvaṃ vidyādharatvamabhikāṃkṣa[te]mamāpi saṃmukhadarśanaṃ tena aṣṭamyāṃ śuklapakṣe nave paṭake acchinnadaśe keśāpagate śucinā citrakareṇa āryāṣṭāṅgopavāsopavasitena aśleṣairaṅgairnavabhājanasthaiścitrāpayitavyam / madhye tathāgatapratimā dharmaṃ deśayamānā dakṣiṇenāryavajrakrodho vajraṃ bhrāmayamānaḥ sarvālaṅkāravibhūṣitaḥ[puṣpa]mālyārdhacandrahāraḥ śvetavastraprāvṛtaḥ vāmapārśve anopamā śarakāṇḍagaurī sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitā śvetavastrā padmahastā samāśvāsayaṃtī / tataḥ śucinā vidyādhareṇa āryāṣṭāṅgopavasitena śucau sadhātuke tathāgatasthāne kṣīrayāvakāhāreṇa śvetavastraprāvṛtenātmadvitīyena aṣṭamyāṃ pūrvasecaṃ kṛtvā nānāpuṣpagandhadhūpadīpaiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā triskṛtvā tryaṣṭaśatiko jāpo dātavyaḥ / ekaikaṃ sumanaḥpuṣpaṃ jāpya tryaṣṭaśataiḥ sā pratimā āhartavyā tathāgatasya vajrapāṇeśca pūrvataraṃ puṣpadhūpagandhaṃ dātavyam / balipāyasadadhyodanaṃ nānārasaṃ nānāmadyaṃ
body.translated_text: Whoever desires the qualities of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, desires wealth and grain, desires the subjugation of all beings, aspires to great sovereignty in existence, kingship, or the state of a <s>vidyādhara</s> (spell-master), and wishes to behold me face to face — by such a person, on the eighth day of the bright fortnight, on a new cloth with uncut edges and free of hair, by a pure painter who has observed the noble eightfold <s>upoṣadha</s> (fast), with unblemished limbs, using pigments placed in new vessels, an image should be painted. In the center, a <s>Tathāgata</s> image teaching the <s>Dharma</s>; on the right, the Noble <s>Vajrakrodha</s> brandishing a <s>vajra</s>, adorned with all ornaments, wearing flower garlands, a half-moon necklace, and clad in white garments; on the left, <s>Anopamā</s>, fair as a reed stalk, adorned with all ornaments, clad in white, holding a lotus in her hand, offering reassurance. Then, a pure <s>vidyādhara</s> who has observed the noble eightfold fast, in a clean place with relics, in a <s>Tathāgata</s> shrine, subsisting on milk and barley food, clad in white garments, together with one companion, on the eighth day, having first made an ablution, having made offerings with various flowers, incense, fragrances, and lamps, a recitation of three hundred and eight should be given three times. Having recited three hundred and eight times over each <s>sumanas</s> (jasmine) flower, that image should be brought forth, and flowers, incense, and fragrance should first be offered to the <s>Tathāgata</s> and <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>. An oblation of <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice), curd-rice, various flavors, and various liquors

body.text: caturdiśe kṣeptavyam / pūrṇapañcadaśyāmanenaiva vidhinā baliḥ anyā[ni] ca yathālābhena dhūpakarpūrakundurukacandanamrakṣaṃ dātavyam / sugandhatailena dvau dipau dātavyau / tatrāhaṃ svarūpeṇopatiṣṭhāmi / yathepsitaṃ varaṃ dāsyāmi samādhilābhamākāśagamanamantardhānaṃ rājatvaṃ balacakravartitvaṃ vidyādharatvaṃ nidhivādaṃ dhātuvādaṃ paracittajñānaṃ dīrghāyuṣkatvam / sarvasattvānāṃ maitracittena bhavitavyam / mānakrodhadherṣyāmātsaryaparivarjitena staupikadhārmikasāṃghikārthāpahāraparivarjitena bhavitavyam / tathāgatānāmabhedyaprasādena[bhavitavyam] / yadi cāhaṃ bhagavan pañcānantaryaṃ kariṣyāmi tribhiḥ sādhanairna samanvāherayaṃ mā cāhaṃ bhagavannanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ sace buddhe aprasādalabdho bhave yaśca vimatiprāpto yaścaṃ pāpamakuśalaṃ kṛtvā na viratimanugṛṇhāti kleśopakleśacittastasyāhaṃ cāpi darśanaṃ dāsyāmi lābhamapi kariṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: should be cast in the four directions. On the full-moon fifteenth day, by this same procedure, an oblation should be offered, and other [offerings] according to what is available — incense of camphor, <s>kunduruka</s> (frankincense), and sandalwood ointment should be given. Two lamps should be given with fragrant oil. There I shall appear in my own form. I shall grant whatever desired boon — attainment of <s>samādhi</s>, movement through the sky, disappearance, kingship, sovereignty as a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) of power, the state of a <s>vidyādhara</s>, discovery of hidden treasures, alchemy, knowledge of others' minds, and longevity.

body.text: atha bhagavān sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu bhagini / sādhu khalu punastvaṃ bhagini yattvayā sarvasattvānāmarthāya pāpasamācāreṣu
body.translated_text: One must maintain a mind of loving-kindness toward all beings. One must be free from pride, anger, jealousy, and envy, and must refrain from misappropriating what belongs to <s>stūpas</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, or the <s>Saṅgha</s>. One must have unshakeable faith in the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. If I, <s>Bhagavān</s>, were to commit the five acts of immediate retribution and not accomplish the three means of realization, then may I, <s>Bhagavān</s>, not attain unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). But to one who has obtained lack of faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, who has attained doubt, or who, having committed sin and unwholesome deeds, does not embrace restraint, whose mind is afflicted by <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) and secondary <s>kleśas</s> — to such a one I shall neither grant my vision nor bestow any attainment.

body.text: sattveṣu imā evaṃrūpā mantrapadā bhāṣitāḥ pratijñā kṛtā / śakṣyasi tvamanayā evaṃrūpayā mahākaruṇayā sarvasattvānanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau prati[ṣṭhā]payitum / evameva tvayāpi karaṇīyam /
body.translated_text: beings of evil conduct — you have spoken such <s>mantra</s> words and made this vow. You shall be able, with such great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), to establish all beings in unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Thus indeed should you continue to act.

body.text: atha śaṃkhini mahādevī bhagavantaṃ nānāpuṣpairnānāgandhairabhyarcya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya pādaryonipatya bhagavantametadavocat / ahamapi bhagavaṃstathāgatādhiṣṭhānena pratijñāṃ kariṣyāmi tathāgataśāsanacirasthityartham / teṣāṃ ca dharmabhāṇakānāṃ dharmaśrāvaṇikānāṃ sarvāśāparipūrakarāṇi mantrapadāni dāsyāmi / rakṣāyai tanme bhagavān anujānātu /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śaṅkhinī Mahādevī</s> (the Great Goddess Śaṅkhinī), having worshipped the <s>Bhagavān</s> with various flowers and various fragrances, having circumambulated him, having prostrated at his feet, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these words: I too, <s>Bhagavān</s>, by the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, shall make a vow for the long endurance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching. To those <s>dharmabhāṇakas</s> (preachers of the Dharma) and <s>dharmaśrāvaṇikas</s> (listeners of the Dharma), I shall give <s>mantra</s> words that fulfill all wishes. For their protection, may the <s>Bhagavān</s> give me permission.

body.text: namo namaḥ sarvatathāgatānām / om śaṃkhini devi āgaccha āgaccha / tiṣṭha dhane dhanajaye / vṛ vṛ vṛddhikari / dhṛ dhṛ dhṛtikari / nānāvividhaveśavastrāyudhadhāriṇi / yu yu āyuṣpālani / tathāgatānāṃ smara bodhicittaṃ mā vilamba / dehi me varam / śaṃkhini svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>Namo namaḥ sarvatathāgatānām</s> (Homage, homage to all Tathāgatas)! <s>Oṃ Śaṅkhinī Devī āgaccha āgaccha / tiṣṭha dhane dhanajaye / vṛ vṛ vṛddhikari / dhṛ dhṛ dhṛtikari / nānāvividhaveśavastrāyudhadhāriṇi / yu yu āyuṣpālani / tathāgatānāṃ smara bodhicittaṃ mā vilamba / dehi me varam / Śaṅkhinī svāhā</s> (Oṃ, Goddess Śaṅkhinī, come, come! Abide, O Wealth, O Conqueror of Wealth! Vṛ vṛ, granter of increase! Dhṛ dhṛ, granter of firmness! Bearer of manifold garments, robes, and weapons! Yu yu, protector of life! Remember the awakening mind of the Tathāgatas, do not delay! Grant me a boon! Śaṅkhinī, svāhā!)

body.text: imairmantrapadaiḥ sa bhagavan kāyagatairyaśovṛddhimanuprāpsyati / tejovṛddhiṃ bhogavṛddhim aiśvaryavṛddhiṃ dīrghāyuṣkatāṃ śatruvaśīkaraṇavṛddhimanuprāpsyati / aṣṭaśatajaptena yathālābhena baliṃ dattvā caturdiśe dhūpaṃ kundurukaṃ tathāgatasyodāratarapūjā kartavyā / dīpo
body.translated_text: By these <s>mantra</s> words, <s>Bhagavān</s>, one who carries them on the body will attain increase in fame, increase in splendor, increase in enjoyments, increase in sovereignty, longevity, and increase in the subjugation of enemies. Having recited eight hundred times and having offered an oblation according to what is available in the four directions, incense of <s>kunduruka</s> (frankincense) [should be offered], and a most excellent worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> should be performed. A lamp
