body.text: dātavyaḥ / ekaviṃśatidivasāni maitravihāriṇā niyamasthena bhavitavyam / tataḥ sarvābhiprāyaṃ paripūrayiṣyāmi saddharmapratikṣepakaṃ sthāpya / śucau pradeśe kartavyaṃ devāyatane vā / atha bhagavān sā ca yathāsamāgatā parṣa sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu bhagini / subhāṣitamidam / pratijñā bahuguṇasamanvāgatā / evameva tvamapi karaṇīyamanāgate 'dhvani /
body.translated_text: should be given. For twenty-one days, one must abide in a state of loving-kindness and observe the vows. Then I shall fulfill all desires, except for one who rejects the True <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>). It should be performed in a clean place or in a temple. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the assembly that had gathered gave their approval: Well done, well done, sister! This is well spoken. Your vow is endowed with many virtues. Thus indeed should you continue to act in the future.

body.text: VI
body.translated_text: VI

body.text: atha khalu bhīmā mahādevī suvarṇapuṣpairbhagavantamabhyarcya bhagavataścaraṇayornipatya bhagavantametadavocat / ahamapi bhagavaṃsteṣāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāṃ dharmaśrāvaṇikānāṃ teṣāṃ ca lekhakānāṃ teṣāṃ ca dhārakāṇāṃ vācakānāṃ pūjakānāmarthāya sarvāśāparipūrakarāṇi hiraṇyamaṇimuktā bhogaiśvaryarājatvadīrghāyuṣkarāṇi śatruvaśīkaraṇāni mantrapadāni dāsyāmi / yaḥ kaści rājā vā rājñī vā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā vā dhārayiṣyanti satkariṣyanti likhiṣyanti likhāpayiṣyanti tathāgatagurugauraveṇa pratiprattyā yathopadiṣṭāḥ pratipatsyante tasyāhaṃ bhagavan rakṣiṣyāmi paripālanaṃ kariṣyāmi yathocitaṃ varaṃ dāsyāmi bhogaiśvaryairavaikalyaṃ kariṣyāmi vivādayuddhaḍimbaḍamare jayaṃ kariṣyāmi / āyuḥsaṃpadamupasaṃhariṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhīmā Mahādevī</s> (the Great Goddess Bhīmā), having worshipped the <s>Bhagavān</s> with golden flowers and having prostrated at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these words: I too, <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the sake of those <s>dharmabhāṇakas</s> (preachers of the Dharma), <s>dharmaśrāvaṇikas</s> (listeners of the Dharma), those scribes, those who retain, those who recite, and those who worship — I shall give <s>mantra</s> words that fulfill all wishes, that bestow gold, jewels, pearls, enjoyments, sovereignty, kingship, and longevity, and that subjugate enemies. Whoever — be it a king, a queen, a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, an <s>upāsaka</s>, or an <s>upāsikā</s> — shall hold them, honor them, write them, or cause them to be written, and with reverence for the <s>Tathāgata</s> as guru, shall practice as instructed — to such a one, <s>Bhagavān</s>, I shall grant protection, I shall provide safeguarding, I shall give appropriate boons, I shall ensure no lack of enjoyments and sovereignty, I shall grant victory in disputes, wars, conflicts, and tumults, and I shall bestow the attainment of long life.

body.text: tasya ca viṣayasya nagarasya paripālanaṃ kariṣyāmi / tanme bhagavānanujānātu /
body.translated_text: And I shall provide protection to that territory and city. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> give me permission for this.

body.text: namaḥ sarvatathāgatānāṃ sarvabodhisattvānām āryāvalokiteśvaravajrapāṇiprabhṛtīnām /
body.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, to all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, to the Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, and the rest.

body.text: om mahādevi bhīme bhīmamate / jaye jayāvahe / yaśajave tejajave / vyākaraṇaprāpte sarvasattvāvalokane kṛpatejabahule tathāgatānujñātaṃ pālaya / smara pratijñām / buddhādhiṣṭhānena dehi me varam / siddhiṃ kuru / devi mahādevi satyavacanadevi bhīme satyavacanapratiṣṭhite guhyanivāsini svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ Mahādevī Bhīme Bhīmamate / jaye jayāvahe / yaśajave tejajave / vyākaraṇaprāpte sarvasattvāvalokane kṛpatejabahule tathāgatānujñātaṃ pālaya / smara pratijñām / buddhādhiṣṭhānena dehi me varam / siddhiṃ kuru / Devī Mahādevī satyavacanadevi Bhīme satyavacanapratiṣṭhite guhyanivāsini svāhā</s> (Oṃ, Great Goddess <s>Bhīmā</s>, O Fierce-minded One! Victory, bearer of victory! Swift in fame, swift in splendor! Having obtained prophecy, gazer upon all beings, abounding in the splendor of compassion — protect what has been authorized by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>! Remember the vow! By the empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>, grant me a boon! Bestow accomplishment! O Goddess, Great Goddess, Goddess of True Speech, <s>Bhīmā</s>, established in truthful speech, dweller in the secret, <s>svāhā</s>!)

body.text: imāni tāni bhagavan mantrapadāni tathāgatādhiṣṭhitāni tathāgatānujñātāni mayā bhāṣitāni sattvānāmarthāya / yaṃ yameva kāmaṃ manasikṛtvā japiṣyate tathāgatasya purataḥ puṣpadhūpagandhadīpaiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā pāyasarasabaliṃ caturdiśe dattvā taṃ tameva aṣṭaśatajāpena sarvāśāṃ paripūrayiṣyāmi / yaḥ kaści māṃ svarūpeṇābhikāṃkṣī bhave tena acchinnadaśe keśāpagate aśleṣairaṅgairnavabhājanasthairaṣṭasyām āryāṣṭāṃgaparigṛhītena citrakareṇa citrāpayitavyā śarakāṇḍagaurī sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitāṃgī śvetavastrā madhye tathāgatapratimā dha[rma deśa]yamānā dakṣiṇenāryāvalokiteśvaraḥ sāṃkathyaṃ kurvan vāmapārśve bhīmā mahādevī
body.translated_text: These, <s>Bhagavān</s>, are the <s>mantra</s> words empowered by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, authorized by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, spoken by me for the benefit of beings. Whatever wish one contemplates while reciting before the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having made offerings with flowers, incense, fragrances, and lamps, having offered an oblation of <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) and flavored foods in the four directions — that very wish I shall fulfill by a recitation of eight hundred. Whoever desires to behold me in my own form — by such a person, on a cloth with uncut edges and free of hair, by a painter who has undertaken the noble eightfold [fast], with unblemished limbs, using [pigments] placed in new vessels, on the eighth day, an image should be painted: <s>Bhīmā</s>, fair as a reed stalk, with limbs adorned with all ornaments, clad in white; in the center, a <s>Tathāgata</s> image teaching the <s>Dharma</s>; on the right, the Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> engaged in conversation; on the left, <s>Bhīmā Mahādevī</s>

body.text: kuṇḍiganetṛkaparigṛhītā samāśvāsayantī / tato 'ṣṭamyāṃ pūrvasecaṃ kṛtvā puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanaiḥ sadhātuke caityasthāne balipāyasadadhyodanaṃ caturdiśe yāvat pūrṇapañcadarśīṃ śūcinā vidyādhareṇa udāratarāṃ puṣpadhūpagandhadīpaiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtva baliṃ dattvā nānārasairanyāni ca yathālābhena śuklabaliṃ dattvā sarvasattvānāṃ maitracittena dayācittena bhūtvā jātīpuṣpā[ṇāma]ṣṭabhiḥ śataiḥ sā pratimā āhartavyā / ekaikaṃ japya tatrāhaṃ svarūpeṇopatiṣṭhiṣyāmi yathepsitaṃ varaṃ dāsyāmi rājyaiśvaryam ākāśagamanaṃ nidhivādaṃ dhātuvādaṃ vidyādharatvam anyāni ca yathepsitāni karmāṇi kariṣyāmi akālamṛtyupratiṣedhanaṃ sarvarogapraśamanaṃ paracakrapramardanaṃ putralambham arthāgamanaṃ prītiṃ sarvasattveṣu / yadi cāhaṃ bhagavan pañcānantaryaṃ kariṣyāmi na sarvāśāṃ paripūrayeyaṃ mā cāhaṃ bhagavannanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyaṃ saddharmapratikṣepakaṃ sthāpya yaśca vicikitsāprāpto buddhadharmasaṃghe / bhagavānāha / sādhu sādhu bhagini sādhu khalu punastvaṃ bhagini yattvaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ hitāya sukhāya pratipannā asyaiva ca dharmaparyāyasya cirasthityarthaṃ
body.translated_text: held by a <s>kuṇḍiga</s>-vessel and a guide, reassuring [them]. Then, on the eighth day, having performed the preliminary sprinkling, at a shrine containing relics, with flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, and ointments, one should offer <s>bali</s> (ritual offering) of rice-pudding and curd-rice in the four directions. Until the full moon of the fifteenth day, a pure <s>vidyādhara</s> (knowledge-holder), having performed a most excellent worship with flowers, incense, fragrances, and lamps, having given <s>bali</s> with various flavors and other things as available, having given a pure white offering, having become benevolent-minded and compassionate toward all beings — that image should be invoked with eight hundred <s>jātī</s> (jasmine) flowers. Reciting [the mantra] for each one, there I shall appear in my own form and grant the desired boon — sovereignty, flight through the sky, <s>nidhivāda</s> (treasure-discovery), <s>dhātuvāda</s> (alchemy), <s>vidyādharatva</s> (the state of a knowledge-holder) — and I shall perform other desired deeds: prevention of untimely death, pacification of all diseases, destruction of enemy armies, obtaining a son, acquisition of wealth, and affection among all beings. And if I, <s>Bhagavān</s>, should commit the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) acts or fail to fulfill all wishes, then may I not attain unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) — excepting those who reject the true <s>Dharma</s> and those who have arrived at doubt regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Excellent! Excellent, sister! Excellent indeed are you, sister, in that you have set out for the benefit and happiness of all beings, and for the long endurance of this very <s>Dharma</s> discourse

body.text: pratipannā / tena hi bhagini nityameva imāḥ pratijñāstvayā nityameva samanvāhartavyāḥ / atheyaṃ mahāpṛthivī tasmin samaye pracacāla divyañca kusumavarṣamabhiprāvarṣat / sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu subhāṣitamidam / pratijñā sarvasattvānāṃ sarvāśāparipūrikā bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: you have set out. Therefore, sister, these vows must always be constantly maintained by you. Then at that time, this great earth trembled and a divine rain of flowers fell. And that entire assembly gave an exclamation of approval: Excellent! Excellent! This is well spoken! The vow will fulfill all the wishes of all beings.

body.text: VII
body.translated_text: VII

body.text: athāryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarbhagavantametadavocat kiṃ punarbhagavan sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā likhanavācanalikhāpanasaṃprakāśanapaṭhanasvādhyayanapūjanasaṃprakāśanayā puṇyamanuprāpsyati imasya dharmaparyāyasya / bhagavānāha / tena hi tvāmevāryāvalokiteśvara pariprakṣyāmi yathe te kṣamaṃ tathā vyākuru / avalokiteśvara āha / bhagavāneva vyākurutāṃ nāsti tathāgatasya adṛṣṭaṃ vā aśrutaṃ vā avijñātaṃ vā / bhagavānāha / yaśca kulaputra asya dharmaparyāyasya likhanalikhāpanavācanapūjanasaṃprakāśanapaṭhanasvādhyayanāt puṇyamanuprāpsyati sa upamenāpi na śakyaṃ varṇayitum / tat kasya hetoḥ / sarvasattvānāṃ yathābhiprāyaparipūrakam / dānaṃ dattvā te sattvā aparimuktā eva bhavanti jarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadauramanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ / varṣatasahasraṃ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ kriḍāpayitvā aparimuktā eva te sattvā bhavanti narakatiryagyoniyamalokapretaviṣayeṣu punarapi duḥkhānyanubhavanti / asya dharmaparyāyasya śravaṇaṃ sattvebhyaḥ kṛtvā pūjanaṃ saṃprakāśanaṃ[ca]kṛtvā arthaṃ cāsyāvaśrutya
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> again spoke to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: What merit, <s>Bhagavān</s>, will that son or daughter of good family obtain through writing, reciting, having it written, proclaiming, studying, self-study, worshipping, and elucidating this <s>Dharma</s> discourse? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Then I shall question you yourself, Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> — answer as seems fitting to you. <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> said: Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself answer, for there is nothing unseen, unheard, or unknown by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Son of good family, the merit that one shall obtain from writing, having written, reciting, worshipping, proclaiming, studying, and practicing self-study of this <s>Dharma</s> discourse cannot be described even by analogy. For what reason? Because it fulfills the wishes of all beings according to their intentions. Even after giving gifts, those beings are still not liberated from old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair. Even after letting them enjoy the five strands of sensual pleasure for a thousand years, those beings are still not liberated — in the realms of hells, animal births, the world of <s>Yama</s>, and the domain of hungry ghosts, they experience suffering again. But having caused beings to hear this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, having worshipped and proclaimed it, and having understood its meaning

body.text:
pratipattyā pratipadya parimuktā eva bhavanti jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhya sarvanarakatiryagyoniyamalokebhyaḥ / tasmāt tathāgata ayaṃ puṇyaskandha upamenāpi pramāṇaṃ na kurvanti / yaśca kulaputra asya ca dharmaparyāyasyoddiśya sarṣapaphalamātrakaṃ ca hiraṇyasya ekapuṣpaṃ vā ekaphalaṃ vā ekapatākāṃ vā vādyaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā vastraṃ vā āsanaṃ vā ābharaṇaṃ vā parityaje likhe likhāpaye dhāraye vācaye pūjaye satkare parebhyaśca viastareṇa saṃprakāśaye taṃ ca dharmabhāṇakaṃ vācaye pūjaye yaśca tiṣṭhate tathāgate saṃmukhapūjayā saparṣa pūjaye mānaye sarvasukhopadhānena varṣaśatasahasramupatiṣṭhe gandhamālyavilepanairdhvajapatākābhirvihāracaṃkramodyānaṃ kārāpaye ardhayojanocchritaṃ saptaratnamayaṃ stūpaṃ kāraye śataṃ vā sahasraṃ vā tathāgata[muddiśya]tāṃśca divyapūjayā pūjaye varṣaśatasahasram ayaṃ ca tato bahutarapuṇyasaṃskāraṃ syā / asya dharmaparyāyasya likhanalikhāpanadhāraṇapaṭhanapūjanasaṃprakāśanayā na imāṃ
tathāgatasaṃmukhapūjāṃ na tveva sattvebhyo dānaṃ dattvā pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaḥ krīḍāpayitvā / tasmāttarhi taiśca kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhirvā rājarājaputramahāmātrāmātyairvā satatasmitamayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ pūjayitavyaḥ / tathāgatasaṃjñā evotpādayitavyā / teṣāṃ kalyāṇamitrāṇāṃ ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrāvayati kathayati arthaṃ cāsyopasaṃharati taḥ satkṛtya ayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ śrotavya udagrahītavyo dhārayitavyo vācayitavyo manasi kartavyaḥ / evaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam /
body.translated_text: through practice, having practiced, they become completely liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and from all hells, animal births, and the world of <s>Yama</s>. Therefore, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not measure this heap of merit even by analogy. And whoever, son of good family, dedicated to this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, should offer even a mustard-seed's amount of gold, or a single flower, a single fruit, a single banner, music, fragrance, a garment, a seat, or an ornament; who writes, has it written, retains, recites, worships, and honors it; who proclaims it in detail to others; who recites to and worships that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher — and whoever worships and honors a living <s>Tathāgata</s> with face-to-face worship together with his assembly, attends him with all comforts for a hundred thousand years with fragrances, garlands, ointments, flags, and banners, has a monastery, cloister, and garden built, has a <s>stūpa</s> made of the seven precious substances built half a <s>yojana</s> high — a hundred or a thousand [of them] — dedicated to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and worships them with divine worship for a hundred thousand years: this [merit from the <s>Dharma</s> discourse] would be an even greater mass of merit than that. Through writing, having written, retaining, studying, worshipping, and proclaiming this <s>Dharma</s> discourse — [the merit] surpasses this face-to-face worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and even surpasses giving gifts to beings and letting them enjoy the five strands of sensual pleasure. Therefore, those sons or daughters of good family, or kings, princes, ministers, and counselors should constantly worship this <s>Dharma</s> discourse. The perception of the <s>Tathāgata</s> itself should be generated [toward it]. Toward those spiritual friends who cause [them] to hear this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, teach it, and convey its meaning — with reverence, this <s>Dharma</s> discourse should be heard, taken up, retained, recited, and reflected upon in the mind. Thus the thought should be generated:

body.text: lābhā asmābhiḥ sulabdhāḥ / yo 'smābhiḥ śrutam apathagāmināṃ pathamupadarśayati anarthe arthasaṃjñinām anitye nityasaṃjñinām asukhe sukhasaṃjñināṃ yadasmābhirnarakatiryogyoniyamalokaparimokṣaṇārthaṃ tathāgatakṛtyaṃ kṛtam / avalokiteśvara āha / mahākṛtyena tathāgatakṛtyena imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ prakāśitam /
body.translated_text: 'Gains have been well gained by us! What has been heard by us shows the path to those going astray, to those who perceive meaning in the meaningless, who perceive permanence in the impermanent, who perceive happiness in what is not happiness. For our liberation from hells, animal births, and the world of <s>Yama</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s deed has been accomplished.' <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> said: By this great deed, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s deed, this <s>Dharma</s> discourse has been proclaimed to all beings.

body.text: bhagavānāha / ayaṃ ca kulaputra dharmaparyāyaḥ paścime kāle paścime samaye dakṣiṇāpathe pracariṣyati tatrāpi bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikārājarājaputramahāmātrāmātyā bhājanībhūtāḥ pūjakā dhārakā vācakā bhaviṣyanti śraddhāsyanti pattīṣyanti / sa ce uttarapūrvapaścimāyāṃ pracare tat parakarmābhiyuktāste sattvā bhaviṣyanti na śroṣyanti śraddhāsyanti na pattīṣyanti na pūjayiṣyanti hīnavīryanaṣṭasmṛtayo nānāvyākṣepakuṭambadāsadāsībhogaiśvaryahāsyalāsyanāṭyanṛtyagīterṣyāmātsaryasmṛtayo na śroṣyanti na pattīṣyanti napūjayiṣyanti te aparimuktā eva jarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhya pretayamalokaviṣayebhyo bhaviṣyanti / tasmāttarhi taiḥ kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhirvā sarvāpāyairātmānaṃ parimoktukāmena satkṛtya ayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ pūjayitavyo dhārayitavyaḥ satkartavyaḥ parebhyaḥ saṃprakāśatitavyo manasā dhārayitavyaḥ / ḍimbaḍumaraduḥsvapnadurnimitteṣu akālamṛtyugomarapaśumaramānuṣamarebhyo nānāvyādhibhayopadravebhya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ pūjayitvā vācayitavyaḥ dhvaje vā ucchrapitaṃ kṛtvā pūjayitvā nānāgandhapuṣpadhūpavādyaiḥ praceṣṭavyaḥ / caturdiśe baliṃ īttvābhinamaskṛtya puṣpadhūpagandhaiḥ sarva ityupadravāḥ praśamaṃ yāsyanti /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: And this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, son of good family, in the final age, in the final time, will spread in the southern region. There too, <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, <s>upāsikās</s>, kings, princes, ministers, and counselors will become worthy vessels, worshippers, retainers, and reciters — they will have faith and will believe. But if it spreads in the north, east, or west, those beings will be devoted to other activities; they will not listen, will not have faith, will not believe, will not worship — being of weak effort and lost mindfulness, their mindfulness overwhelmed by various distractions: family, male servants, female servants, enjoyments, power, laughter, dance, theater, acting, singing, jealousy, and miserliness — they will not listen, will not believe, will not worship. They will remain unliberated from old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and from the realms of hungry ghosts and the world of <s>Yama</s>. Therefore, those sons or daughters of good family, desiring to free themselves from all lower realms, should respectfully worship, retain, and honor this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, proclaim it to others, and retain it in the mind. In times of disturbances, tumults, bad dreams, and evil omens, against untimely death, cattle plague, animal plague, and human plague, against various diseases, fears, and calamities, having worshipped this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, it should be recited; or having raised it on a banner and worshipped it with various fragrances, flowers, incense, and music, one should make efforts. Having given <s>bali</s> (ritual offerings) in the four directions and prostrated with flowers, incense, and fragrances, all calamities will be pacified.

body.text: atha bhagavān tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: sarvasya sattvasya anugrahārthaṃ
children.translated_text: For the benefit of all beings,

children.text: yā bhāṣitā pūrvabhaveṣu nāyakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: that which was spoken by the leaders in former lives —

children.text: ahaṃ tathā tvāmapi deśayiṣye
children.translated_text: I shall likewise teach you also —

children.text: gṛṇhāhi ānanda imaṃ samādhim || 1 ||
children.translated_text: receive, O <s>Ānanda</s>, this <s>samādhi</s>!

body.text: yaścaiva traidhātukadānu dadyā saptāna ratnāna ca pūrayitvā /
body.translated_text: And whoever should give a gift, filling the three realms with the seven precious substances,

body.text: buddheṣu dharmeṣu sadāpramattaḥ upamāpi tasya na sa bhonti dānam || 2 ||
body.translated_text: always diligent toward the <s>Buddhas</s> and the <s>Dharma</s> — even by comparison, that gift does not [equal this].

children.text: yaścaiva buddheṣvabhiśraddadhitvā vihārakārāpayi caityakāni /
children.translated_text: And whoever, having placed faith in the <s>Buddhas</s>, has monasteries and shrines built,

children.text: yaścaiva sūtraṃ[ca] dhareti kaści ayaṃ tato bahutaru puṇyu bheṣyate || 3 ||
children.translated_text: and whoever retains this <s>sūtra</s> — this one's merit shall be far greater than that.

children.text: yaścāpi ekaṃ kṣipayeta puṣpaṃ vastraṃ ca mālyaṃ ca vilepanaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: And whoever would offer even a single flower, a garment, a garland, or ointment likewise,

children.text: imaṃ samādhiṃ ca[ya] satkareta nāyaṃ tato bahutaru puṇyu bhoti || 4 ||
children.translated_text: and whoever honors this <s>samādhi</s> — indeed, this one's merit becomes far greater than that.

children.text: yaścāpi kārṣāpaṇu dānu dadyā imasya sūtrasya ca pūjanārtham /
children.translated_text: And whoever gives even a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> (small coin) as a gift for the worship of this <s>sūtra</s> —

children.text: janitvā bodhāya ca maitracitte ayaṃ tato bahutaru puṇyu prāpnuyā || 5 ||
children.translated_text: having generated the mind of loving-kindness for awakening, one would thereby obtain much greater merit. // Verse 5 //

children.text: yaścāpi sattveṣu imaṃ samādhiṃ prakāśaye deśayi bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: And whatever <s>bodhisattva</s> would illuminate and teach this <s>samādhi</s> among beings,

children.text: pratipādaye bodhimanuttare tathā upamāpi puṇyaṃpi na tasya bhoti || 6 ||
children.translated_text: and thus guide them toward unsurpassed awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — there is no comparison for that one's merit. // Verse 6 //

body.text: imaṃ ca śrutvā tatha ānuśaṃsāḥ kṛtvā ca maitraṃ tatha sarvasattvaiḥ /
body.translated_text: Having heard these benefits and having practiced loving-kindness toward all beings,

body.text: tasmāpi sūtram imu dhārayeta likheta vāceta tathā prakāśaye || 7 ||
body.translated_text: therefore one should retain this <s>sūtra</s>, write it, recite it, and illuminate it. // Verse 7 //

children.text: jarāvyādhimṛtyu[bhistathātitīvraiḥ śataiścaduḥkhaiḥ] paripīḍitāśca /
children.translated_text: Those tormented by old age, disease, death, and by hundreds of extremely intense sufferings,

children.text: upapadyamānā narakeṣu pretayo mā paścakāle parītāpyu bheṣyatha || 8 ||
children.translated_text: being reborn in hells and as hungry ghosts (<s>pretas</s>) — do not, in the final time, become overcome with anguish! // Verse 8 //

children.text: sa mṛtyukāle bhayabhītamānasaḥ abhīkṣṇamucchvāsanamucchvasantaḥ /
children.translated_text: At the time of death, with a mind terrified by fear, breathing with labored gasps,

children.text: kosmābhi trāṇaṃ bhavate parāyaṇaṃ mukhe mukhaṃ prekṣati bālabuddhiḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: who will be the refuge and shelter? The one of childish understanding gazes face to face [at death]. // Verse 9 //

children.text: yasmā tathāgatamabhipūjayitvā
children.translated_text: Since, not having worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>, nor the <s>Saṅgha</s>,

children.text: bauddhaṃ ca dharmaṃ tatha sāṃghikañca /
hariṣya neṣye yamaloki dāruṇe na tasya trāṇaṃ sada kaści bheṣyati || 10 ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Yama</s>'s messengers] will carry and lead one to the terrible world of <s>Yama</s> — no one will ever be a protector for that one. // Verse 10 //

children.text: na putradāraṃ na ca mitrabāndhavān na cāpi rāṣṭraṃ na ca hāsyalāsyam /
children.translated_text: Neither sons nor wife, neither friends nor relatives, neither the kingdom nor laughter and dance,

children.text: dhanaṃ na dhānyaṃ na ca vastrabhūṣaṇaṃ sarvaṃ jahitvā puna duḥkhadāruṇam || 11 ||
children.translated_text: neither wealth nor grain, nor garments and ornaments — having abandoned all, one faces terrible suffering again. // Verse 11 //

body.text: imaṃ samādhiṃ na ca śraddadhitvā tathā[ca duḥkhaṃ]dāruṇaṃ vedayate /
body.translated_text: Not having faith in this <s>samādhi</s>, one experiences such terrible suffering;

body.text: ima duḥkhu śrutvā imu ānuśaṃsāḥ ko bālabuddhirna jane prasādam || 12 ||
body.translated_text: having heard of this suffering and these benefits, what person of childish understanding would not generate faith? // Verse 12 //

children.text: tasmācca tairhi sada bhikṣubhikṣuṇī upāsakopāsikarājabhiḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, <s>upāsikās</s>, and kings, always

children.text: imaṃ ca sūtraṃ sada dhārayitvā satkāru nityaṃ ca kartavyadhārake || 13 ||
children.translated_text: this <s>sūtra</s> should always be retained, and constant honor should be rendered to the one who holds it. // Verse 13 //

body.text: athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat / udgṛhītaṃ mayā bhagavan imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śāstṛsaṃjñayā dhārayiṣyāmi pūjayiṣyāmi sarvasattvebhyaḥ saṃprakāśayiṣyāmi / bhagavānāha / yadi tvamānanda yanmayā dharmo bhāṣitaḥ śruto dhārayituṃ tat sarvaṃ na dhāraye na vācaye na pūjaye na vaistārikīkuryā tvayā mama nāparādhye na cāśuśrūṣā kṛtā bhave na cāśrāvakatvam / yaśca imaṃ dharmaparyāya na dhāraye
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these words: I have grasped it, <s>Bhagavān</s>. I shall retain this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse of the Dharma) with the perception of the Teacher; I shall honor it and illuminate it for all beings. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: If you, <s>Ānanda</s>, were to not retain, not recite, not honor, and not propagate all the <s>Dharma</s> that I have spoken and that has been heard — you would not be offending me, nor would you have failed in obedience, nor would it be a failure of discipleship. But whoever does not retain this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>,

body.text: na vācaye na pūjaye na saṃprakāśaye na manasikuryā sa mām aparādhye aśuśrūṣā kṛtā bhave aśrāvakatvaṃ bhave / tasmāttarhi tvamānanda satkṛtya ayaṃ dharmaparyāyo dhārayitavyaḥ / ayaṃ te tathāgatasyānuttarasamyaksaṃbodhatathāgatakṛtyaṃ kariṣyati paścime kāle paścime samaye sarvasattvānām /
body.translated_text: does not recite it, does not honor it, does not illuminate it, and does not attend to it mentally — that person offends me, that person has failed in obedience, that person has failed in discipleship. Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> should be retained with reverence. This [discourse] will accomplish the work of the <s>Tathāgata</s> for your attainment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s unsurpassed perfect awakening — it will serve all beings in the final age, in the final time.

body.text: asmin khalu punardharmaparyāye bhagavatā bhāṣyamāṇe ṣaṣṭīnāṃ prāṇisahasrāṇāmanupādāyāsravebhyaścittāni vimuktāni saptānāṃ śatānāṃ bodhisattvasamādhipratilaṃbho 'bhūt / pañcānāṃ śatānāṃ nānābuddhakṣetravyākaraṇapratilaṃbho 'bhūt / navatīnāṃ prāṇisahasrāṇāṃ sarvakleśavinirmuktāḥ sarvākṣaṇāpāyadurgatayaḥ prahīṇāḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, while this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> was being spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the minds of sixty thousand beings were liberated from the outflows without any further clinging. Seven hundred <s>bodhisattvas</s> attained <s>samādhi</s>. Five hundred received prophecies [of future awakening] in various <s>Buddha</s>-fields. Ninety thousand beings were completely freed from all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), and all states of misfortune, evil destinies, and unfavorable rebirths (<s>akṣaṇa</s>, <s>apāya</s>, <s>durgati</s>) were eliminated.

body.text: athāryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarbhagavantametadavocat / ayaṃ bhagavan dharmaparyāyaḥ paścimakāle paścimasamaye teṣāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ śrotṝṇāṃ dhārayitṝṇāṃ mānayitṝṇāṃ teṣāṃ ca lekhakānāṃ tathāgatakṛtyaṃ kariṣyati / vyākṛtāste yathepsiteṣu nānābuddhakṣetreṣu / ye ca sattvāḥ paścime kāle paścime[sama]ye hāsyanāṭyagītavāditeṣu nānāvyākṣepabahulā rāgadveṣamohāndhā ratikrīḍāsaṃjñinaḥ anitye nityasaṃjñinaḥ īrṣyāmātsaryadauḥśīlyaparigṛhītā na pūjayiṣyanti na mānayiṣyanti na śraddhāsyanti na pattīyiṣyanti na dhārayiṣyanti na śroṣyanti na pratipattyā pratipatsyante / te taṃ pūrvakarmaśubhaphalaṃ parikṣepaṃ kṛtvā nānāduḥkhadaurmanasyaṃ
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> again addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these words: This <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the final age, in the final time, will accomplish the work of the <s>Tathāgata</s> for those sons of good family who hear it, retain it, and honor it, and for those who write it. They are prophesied [to be reborn] in whatever <s>Buddha</s>-fields they desire. But those beings who in the final age, in the final time, are engrossed in manifold diversions of laughter, theater, song, and music, blinded by passion, hatred, and delusion, perceiving amusement and play [as worthwhile], perceiving the impermanent as permanent, seized by jealousy, envy, and moral corruption — they will not honor it, will not respect it, will not have faith, will not believe, will not retain it, will not listen, and will not practice in accordance with the teaching. They, having squandered the wholesome fruit of their former <s>karma</s>, with various sufferings and mental anguish

body.text: nārakaṃ duḥkhamanubhaviṣyanti / tataste anekāni kalpakoṭīśatāniduḥkhamanubhavitvā narakatiryagyoniyamalokeṣu vopapatsyante / dīrgharātramakalyāṇamitravaśāḥ paścānutāpino bhaviṣyanti imaṃ kṣaṇaṃ virāgayitvā / tasmāttarhi kāya[vāṅma]naḥsaṃvareṇa bhavitavyam / buddhadharmasaṃghe[a]bhedyaprasādena sarvasattveṣu maitracittena īrṣyāmātsaryadauḥśīlyacittaparivarjitena krodhaparivarjitena bhavitavyam /
body.translated_text: will experience the suffering of the hells. Then, having experienced suffering for many hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> in the hells, the animal realm, and the world of <s>Yama</s>, they will be reborn there. For a long time, under the power of unwholesome companions, they will be filled with subsequent remorse, having let this opportunity pass. Therefore, one must maintain restraint of body, speech, and mind; one must have unshakeable faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s>; one must maintain a mind of loving-kindness toward all beings; and one must be free from jealousy, envy, moral corruption, and anger.

body.text: atha sā yathāsamāgatā parṣa taistaiḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraiḥ tathāgataṃ pūjayati sma / divyapuṣpagandhamālyavilepanavastrābharaṇaiḥ kilikili prakṣveḍitaśabdaiśca divyatūryatāḍāvacarasaṃgīteḥ sādhukāraṃ pradadau / tad yathā sādhu sādhu bhagavan subhāṣitamidaṃ mahādharmaparyāyaṃ sarvasattvānāmarthāya tathāgataśāsanacirasthityartham /
body.translated_text: Then that assembly which had gathered together worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s> with their respective meritorious preparations — with divine flowers, fragrances, garlands, ointments, garments, and ornaments, with <s>kilikili</s> sounds and exclamations, and with divine musical instruments, cymbals, and songs — and gave their approval: Well done, well done, <s>Bhagavān</s>! This great <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse of the Dharma) has been well spoken, for the benefit of all beings and for the long endurance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching.

body.text: athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat / kiṃnāmāyaṃ bhagavan dharmaparyāyaḥ kathaṃ ca vayaṃ bhagavan dhārayāmaḥ / bhagavānāha / tasmāttarhi tvamānanda imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sarvatathāgatajñānabodhisattvabhūmikramaṇamityapi nāma dhāraya / ṛddhivikurvāṇamahātmasannipātamityapi nāma dhāraya / sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānasattvāvalokanabuddhakṣetrasandarśanavyūhamityapi nāma dhāraya / idamavocad bhagavān / āttamānāḥ āryāvalokiteśvaramaṃjuśrīvajrapāṇiprabhṛtayaḥ sarve bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarve ca mahāśrāvakāḥ sarve ca śakrabrahmalokapālāścatvāraśca
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these words: What is the name of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>? And how should we retain it, <s>Bhagavān</s>? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, retain this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> under the name '<s>Sarvatathāgatajñāna-bodhisattvabhūmikramaṇa</s>' (The Traversal of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> Stages through the Knowledge of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>). Also retain it under the name '<s>Ṛddhivikurvāṇa-mahātmasannipāta</s>' (The Assembly of Great Beings with Miraculous Powers). Also retain it under the name '<s>Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhāna-sattvāvalokana-buddhakṣetrasandarśana-vyūha</s>' (The Array of the Empowerment of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the Beholding of Beings, and the Vision of <s>Buddha</s>-fields). Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Delighted, the Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, and the other foremost ones, all the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, all the great <s>śrāvakas</s>, and all <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the world-protectors (<s>lokapālas</s>), and the four

body.text: mahārājā mahāyakṣiṇyaḥ anaupamyā vimalaprabhā[prabhāvatībhīmāśrīśaṃkhinīharitāmahādevī]prabhṛtayo devanāgayakṣagandharvāsura[garuḍakinnaramahoragāḥ] / sā ca sarvāvatī parṣayathāsamāgatā bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandya[sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu bhagavan] / [iti sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānasattvavalokanabuddhakṣetrasandarśanavyūham nāma mahāyānasūtram] /
body.translated_text: great kings, the great <s>yakṣiṇīs</s> — <s>Anaupamyā</s>, <s>Vimalaprabhā</s>, <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, <s>Bhīmāśrī</s>, <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>Haritā Mahādevī</s>, and the other foremost ones — the <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, and that entire assembly which had gathered together, having rejoiced at what the <s>Bhagavān</s> had spoken, gave their approval: Well done, well done, <s>Bhagavān</s>! [Thus concludes the <s>Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhāna-sattvāvalokana-buddhakṣetrasandarśana-vyūha</s>, a <s>Mahāyāna sūtra</s>.]
